procedures.endpoint.title: Endpoint analysis
procedures.endpoint.short: Programs running on computers, and their alerts
procedures.endpoint.description: Examine endpoint telemetry for unusual processes, parent-child relationships and changes to the host.
procedures.endpoint.question: Which process ran, under whose identity, and what changed?
procedures.identity.title: Identity audit
procedures.identity.description: Correlate authentication records, group membership and account changes across the identity platform.
procedures.identity.question: Are these sign-ins and privileges consistent with normal activity?
procedures.network.title: Network analysis
procedures.network.short: Traffic between systems inside the network
procedures.network.description: Review network flows and packet metadata to identify unusual destinations or movement between systems.
procedures.network.question: Which systems communicated, and does that path make sense?
procedures.firewall.title: Firewall review
procedures.firewall.short: Connections in and out at the network edge
procedures.firewall.description: Inspect firewall sessions, blocked traffic and remote-access connection records at the relevant boundaries.
procedures.firewall.question: What crossed the boundary, when, and in which direction?
procedures.email.title: Email investigation
procedures.email.description: Review message headers, delivery logs and suspicious attachments associated with the reported activity.
procedures.email.question: Did a message or link carry this part of the activity?
procedures.server.title: Server inspection
procedures.server.short: Server logs, services and scheduled jobs
procedures.server.description: Inspect server application logs, services and configuration changes for unexpected execution or access.
procedures.server.question: Which server-side change or request explains the incident?
procedures.cloud.title: Cloud audit
procedures.cloud.short: Cloud keys, roles and activity logs
procedures.cloud.description: Correlate control-plane audit events, workload identity activity and API permissions in the cloud environment.
procedures.cloud.question: Which identity called which API, and from where?
procedures.dns.title: DNS review
procedures.dns.short: Name lookups and newly seen web domains
procedures.dns.description: Examine resolver records for repetitive lookups, unusual domains and encoded query patterns.
procedures.dns.question: Do the domain queries expose a communication channel?
procedures.hunt.title: Targeted threat hunt
procedures.hunt.short: A search across sources for your reading
procedures.hunt.description: Test a specific hypothesis across endpoint, network, identity and cloud telemetry to identify behaviour missed by alerts.
procedures.hunt.question: What observable behaviour would confirm our current hypothesis?
procedures.forensic.title: Forensic triage
procedures.forensic.short: Close examination of a computer's disk and memory
procedures.forensic.description: Collect and analyse preserved artefacts from a suspected host, including execution traces and configuration changes.
procedures.forensic.question: What durable artefacts reconstruct how access was established or retained?
procedures.intel.title: Intelligence correlation
procedures.intel.short: Comparison with known attacker addresses and tools
procedures.intel.description: Compare observed destinations and suspicious artefacts against available threat intelligence, while checking context.
procedures.intel.question: Does known malicious infrastructure help explain our observations?
attacks.phish.title: Phishing attachment
attacks.phish.clue: A document was opened just before the first computer started behaving strangely.
attacks.phish.evidence: A delivered attachment launched the first malicious program when it was opened.
attacks.vpn.title: Stolen remote-access account
attacks.vpn.clue: A valid remote session falls outside its owner’s normal pattern.
attacks.vpn.evidence: A valid remote-access account was used from an unfamiliar source with no matching activity from its owner.
attacks.web.title: Exploited public application
attacks.web.clue: Odd requests to a public website came just before its server started running unexpected programs.
attacks.web.evidence: Malformed requests to the public application led to the server running attacker commands at the start of the incident.
attacks.token.title: Exposed cloud credential
attacks.token.clue: A key an automated cloud job runs under is being used from outside that job's environment.
attacks.token.evidence: A workload credential was used from outside its approved execution environment.
attacks.supply.title: Compromised software update
attacks.supply.clue: Several computers changed soon after a trusted package was deployed.
attacks.supply.evidence: A signed software update delivered malicious code that ran on several computers.
attacks.oauth.title: Malicious application consent
attacks.oauth.clue: A user-approved application has begun reading data it never accessed before.
attacks.oauth.evidence: A deceptive application was granted delegated access to the user’s data.
attacks.vpn-token.title: Replayed remote session
attacks.vpn-token.clue: One remote session appears from two source addresses minutes apart.
attacks.vpn-token.evidence: A captured remote-access token is replayed to reopen an authenticated path without a fresh sign-in.
attacks.helpdesk.title: Help-desk reset abuse
attacks.helpdesk.clue: A password reset was granted on a call that left no callback record.
attacks.helpdesk.evidence: A password reset was performed for a caller who could not be verified.
attacks.sideload.title: Sideloaded browser extension
attacks.sideload.clue: A workstation began reaching a new analytics domain after a browser change.
attacks.sideload.evidence: A manually installed browser add-on is relaying page content outside the organisation.
attacks.redirect.title: Credential phishing redirect
attacks.redirect.clue: A link in an email led through an unfamiliar web address to a sign-in page.
attacks.redirect.evidence: A delivered link led through a look-alike domain to a credential prompt that captured the user's password.
attacks.removable.title: Removable-media infector
attacks.removable.clue: A computer executed a file with no download or mail trail.
attacks.removable.evidence: Execution begins from removable media on a system with no corresponding download or message delivery.
attacks.mfa.title: Repeated MFA approvals
attacks.mfa.clue: A user accepted several unexpected authentication prompts in a row.
attacks.mfa.evidence: The user approved a sign-in challenge generated by an unfamiliar sign-in attempt.
attacks.vendor.title: Vendor software push
attacks.vendor.clue: A supplier's update arrived outside the agreed time for changes.
attacks.vendor.evidence: A vendor update path is used to introduce unauthorised code outside any approved change.
attacks.apikey.title: Public API key abuse
attacks.apikey.clue: A key found in public code is now calling from a new network.
attacks.apikey.evidence: A client key is being used far beyond its original application and address range.
attacks.share.title: Exposed file share write
attacks.share.clue: A shared folder reachable from the internet received an unexpected upload.
attacks.share.evidence: A file written to an internet-reachable share is executed by the service that accepted the connection.
attacks.kiosk.title: Shared kiosk session takeover
attacks.kiosk.clue: A shared terminal stayed signed in to a privileged profile.
attacks.kiosk.evidence: A shared terminal's authenticated session is reused to drive interactive administration, with no matching sign-in by the named operator.
attacks.lapsed-vpn.title: Lapsed supplier VPN account
attacks.lapsed-vpn.clue: A dormant supplier account reconnected after its access should have ended.
attacks.lapsed-vpn.evidence: An account that was never disabled at the end of an engagement reconnects successfully.
attacks.resolver.title: Resolver redirection
attacks.resolver.clue: Internal system names began pointing to an address outside the organisation.
attacks.resolver.evidence: Internal service names are answered with attacker-controlled addresses instead of their own.
attacks.approver.title: Settlement approver takeover
attacks.approver.clue: A payment approver signs in outside the hours their authority covers.
attacks.approver.evidence: A settlement approver's credentials were in use outside the hours their delegation covers, with no corresponding activity from the approver.
attacks.citizen-portal.title: Citizen portal credential reuse
attacks.citizen-portal.clue: A citizen-facing account reaches functions only staff should hold.
attacks.citizen-portal.evidence: A citizen-facing credential reached staff-side functions it was never entitled to, through a portal that trusts one identity for both audiences.
attacks.engineer-vpn.title: Engineering workstation remote access
attacks.engineer-vpn.clue: An engineering workstation is reached remotely outside any maintenance window.
attacks.engineer-vpn.evidence: An engineering workstation was reached over remote access outside every scheduled maintenance window, using an account that normally only works on site.
attacks.joiner.title: Unclaimed joiner account
attacks.joiner.clue: An account provisioned for a new starter is active before their first day.
attacks.joiner.evidence: An account provisioned ahead of a new starter was active before the joiner ever collected it, from a location unrelated to their office.
attacks.pcs-cred.title: Port community system credential
attacks.pcs-cred.clue: A shipping-line account submits for a line it does not represent.
attacks.pcs-cred.evidence: A port community account submitted on behalf of a shipping line it has no agency agreement with, through the trust every party in the community shares.
attacks.id-broker.title: National identity broker assertion
attacks.id-broker.clue: The national sign-in service vouches for a citizen on a service they never opened.
attacks.id-broker.evidence: An identity assertion was issued for a service the citizen never opened, accepted downstream because every agency trusts the broker rather than the request.
attacks.spray.title: Internal password spraying
attacks.spray.clue: Many failed sign-ins across different accounts are followed by a few that succeed.
attacks.spray.evidence: A single internal source tries common passwords across many accounts, then authenticates successfully.
attacks.remote.title: Remote service execution
attacks.remote.clue: An ordinary workstation is making unusual administrative connections.
attacks.remote.evidence: Remote administrative sessions create processes on additional systems from an ordinary workstation.
attacks.role.title: Cloud role escalation
attacks.role.clue: A workload begins using resources beyond its normal permission boundary.
attacks.role.evidence: An over-permissive role relationship lets the compromised identity assume an elevated cloud role.
attacks.dump.title: Credential theft from memory
attacks.dump.clue: A program read the part of a computer's memory that holds passwords, for no normal reason.
attacks.dump.evidence: Credential material was extracted from a running process to gain additional access.
attacks.session.title: Session token replay
attacks.session.clue: The same user session appears in two incompatible locations.
attacks.session.evidence: A captured session is replayed to reach services beyond the one it was issued for.
attacks.trust.title: Trusted service abuse
attacks.trust.clue: An approved connection between applications is reaching systems it never normally talks to.
attacks.trust.evidence: A trusted integration is used to cross into an environment outside its dependency map.
attacks.kerberoast.title: Service ticket extraction
attacks.kerberoast.clue: A workstation requested access passes for services its user never uses.
attacks.kerberoast.evidence: Service tickets were requested in bulk for service accounts the requesting user never uses, so their passwords can be cracked offline.
attacks.delegation.title: Delegation path abuse
attacks.delegation.clue: An account a service runs under can now act on behalf of far more users than it should.
attacks.delegation.evidence: An unapproved delegation relationship is being used to act on another account's behalf.
attacks.pivot.title: Internal port-forward pivot
attacks.pivot.clue: An internal computer began accepting connections on a channel it does not normally offer.
attacks.pivot.evidence: A local tunnel carries administrative traffic into a segment the host does not normally reach.
attacks.scheduled.title: Deployment job abuse
attacks.scheduled.clue: A routine deployment job ran a task it never carried before.
attacks.scheduled.evidence: An automated deployment account runs commands across systems outside any release.
attacks.vault.title: Secret-vault escalation
attacks.vault.clue: A cloud workload began reading stored secrets outside the path it was assigned.
attacks.vault.evidence: A workload identity retrieves secrets outside the paths it was ever scoped to hold.
attacks.implant.title: In-memory implant handoff
attacks.implant.clue: A program running only in memory, with no file on disk, opened a connection to the outside.
attacks.implant.evidence: Code was loaded directly into a running process, leaving nothing on disk.
attacks.db-cred.title: Database credential reuse
attacks.db-cred.clue: The reporting database is being queried from an application server that never used it before.
attacks.db-cred.evidence: One reused credential authenticates to data stores across separate environments.
attacks.keyreuse.title: Trusted key reuse
attacks.keyreuse.clue: An administrator's login key was used from a computer that never held it.
attacks.keyreuse.evidence: A private key is copied to an unrelated system and used there for access.
attacks.snapshot.title: Cloud snapshot share
attacks.snapshot.clue: A copy of a cloud server's disk was attached to a new machine with no change request behind it.
attacks.snapshot.evidence: A disk snapshot was copied and attached to a new instance inside the account, and the credentials stored on it were read.
attacks.ci.title: Pipeline runner hijack
attacks.ci.clue: A cloud build runner began executing steps outside its repository.
attacks.ci.evidence: Build jobs were edited to run commands of the operator's choosing on the shared runner, using an automation token rather than a person's account.
attacks.wmi.title: Remote management execution
attacks.wmi.clue: Admin tools are starting programs on several computers at once.
attacks.wmi.evidence: Management calls create processes across systems with no administrative relationship.
attacks.proxy.title: Internal proxy relay
attacks.proxy.clue: Outbound traffic now leaves through an internal computer that never relayed traffic before.
attacks.proxy.evidence: A compromised system is relaying traffic on behalf of other hosts.
attacks.entitlement.title: Payment entitlement widening
attacks.entitlement.clue: A payment limit was raised shortly before the cut-off.
attacks.entitlement.evidence: A payment entitlement was widened outside the change calendar, lifting one approver past the threshold that would otherwise require a second signature.
attacks.provisioning.title: Subscriber provisioning access
attacks.provisioning.clue: A cloud account that sets up customer services is changing regions it does not support.
attacks.provisioning.evidence: A provisioning account altered subscriber service entries outside the regions it supports, through the same interface the service desk uses.
attacks.historian.title: Historian query pivot
attacks.historian.clue: The plant's process history is being searched far beyond what a shift report needs.
attacks.historian.evidence: Process history was queried far beyond any shift report, enumerating tag names and asset layout rather than reading values.
attacks.printqueue.title: Print service lateral movement
attacks.printqueue.clue: A printing program is running on computers that have no printers.
attacks.printqueue.evidence: The print service was running on systems that hold no print queue, reaching them through a service everyone trusts and nobody watches.
attacks.tos-access.title: Terminal operating system access
attacks.tos-access.clue: Yard moves are queried from a workstation that never plans them.
attacks.tos-access.evidence: Container yard positions and crane allocations were queried from a workstation with no planning role, reading the operating system that runs the quay.
attacks.mgmt-platform.title: Shared management platform pivot
attacks.mgmt-platform.clue: One management console reaches customers it was never assigned.
attacks.mgmt-platform.evidence: A shared management console was used to reach customer estates outside its assignment, because the platform that administers every tenant trusts one operator identity.
attacks.task.title: Malicious scheduled task
attacks.task.clue: The same unverified program comes back at regular intervals after it is stopped.
attacks.task.evidence: A newly created scheduled task relaunches the attacker’s payload at fixed intervals.
attacks.account.title: Hidden privileged account
attacks.account.clue: An unexplained account appears in a privileged group.
attacks.account.evidence: An unapproved privileged account controlled by the attacker was created and added to an administrative group.
attacks.webshell.title: Web-shell foothold
attacks.webshell.clue: A recently changed file on a web server starts unusual programs.
attacks.webshell.evidence: A server-side file accepts remote commands and keeps access available through the application.
attacks.key.title: Additional access key
attacks.key.clue: A new cloud access key for scripts and tools has no change record behind it.
attacks.key.evidence: A second access key was created to preserve attacker access.
attacks.service.title: Rogue system service
attacks.service.clue: A new service starts before users sign in and survives a reboot.
attacks.service.evidence: A malicious program was installed as a service so that it restarts with the machine.
attacks.federation.title: Federated trust backdoor
attacks.federation.clue: The cloud account's rules for trusting outside sign-ins changed outside the maintenance window.
attacks.federation.evidence: A rogue federation relationship was created to keep privileged access to the cloud estate.
attacks.logon.title: Logon script modification
attacks.logon.clue: A sign-in now runs an extra command for every user on a host.
attacks.logon.evidence: A logon process launches an unsigned payload at every interactive sign-in.
attacks.registry.title: Registry autorun persistence
attacks.registry.clue: A computer's start-up settings now launch a program with no owner record.
attacks.registry.evidence: A launcher is restored at every system start from a persisted configuration entry.
attacks.timer.title: System timer unit
attacks.timer.clue: A scheduled timer on a server restarts an unfamiliar program after each reboot.
attacks.timer.evidence: A scheduled timer re-establishes access with no user present.
attacks.sshkey.title: Authorised key addition
attacks.sshkey.clue: A server accepts a key that appears in no provisioning record.
attacks.sshkey.evidence: An added public key grants unattended administrative access.
attacks.role-trust.title: Cross-account role trust
attacks.role-trust.clue: A cloud role can now be used by an outside cloud account that was never approved.
attacks.role-trust.evidence: A cloud trust policy was changed to admit an attacker-controlled identity.
attacks.mailbox.title: Hidden mailbox rule
attacks.mailbox.clue: Copies of selected messages are being forwarded without user knowledge.
attacks.mailbox.evidence: A mailbox rule forwards matched messages and hides them from their owner.
attacks.resolver-svc.title: Registered resolver service
attacks.resolver-svc.clue: A computer began answering internal name lookups it never handled before.
attacks.resolver-svc.evidence: A host is answering internal name queries it was never authorised to serve, redirecting lookups to attacker-controlled addresses.
attacks.image.title: Rogue container image
attacks.image.clue: A cloud software image was rebuilt with no matching code change.
attacks.image.evidence: An altered container layer starts a hidden process at launch.
attacks.wmi-sub.title: Event subscription persistence
attacks.wmi-sub.clue: A hidden management task on a computer runs every time the system starts.
attacks.wmi-sub.evidence: A permanent event consumer relaunches the payload whenever its trigger fires.
attacks.grant.title: Application grant persistence
attacks.grant.clue: An unused application was given back permission to act for users.
attacks.grant.evidence: A persistent application grant was renewed to keep access.
attacks.githook.title: Repository hook persistence
attacks.githook.clue: Every code change saved to the repository now runs an extra step.
attacks.githook.evidence: A repository hook executes attacker code on the build server at every commit.
attacks.svc-key.title: Second service credential
attacks.svc-key.clue: A cloud service has a second access key that no change request created.
attacks.svc-key.evidence: An extra long-lived cloud key was created to preserve access.
attacks.paysupport.title: Payment-support component tampering
attacks.paysupport.clue: A settlement-support component treats a narrow set of transactions differently.
attacks.paysupport.evidence: A payment-support component was altered so a narrow set of transactions bypasses the validation every other item in the batch receives.
attacks.routepolicy.title: Routing policy reinstatement
attacks.routepolicy.clue: A routing policy returns after it is removed.
attacks.routepolicy.evidence: A routing policy redirecting a narrow prefix range was reinstated after removal by a change job nobody scheduled.
attacks.engstation.title: Engineering station persistence
attacks.engstation.clue: An engineering station reloads a component after it is removed.
attacks.engstation.evidence: An engineering station reinstated a removed component at startup, surviving the rebuild the support team believed had cleared it.
attacks.gpo.title: Policy object persistence
attacks.gpo.clue: An account's extra access keeps coming back the morning after someone removes it.
attacks.gpo.evidence: A management policy re-applied a setting no change record covers, restoring access on every machine in scope each time the policy runs.
attacks.gov-platform.title: Shared government platform persistence
attacks.gov-platform.clue: A component used by several agencies reinstates an account after removal.
attacks.gov-platform.evidence: A component several agencies share reinstated a privileged account after removal, so clearing it in one department restored it in the rest.
attacks.backbone.title: Backbone dependency persistence
attacks.backbone.clue: A lookup service every customer relies on keeps returning an extra entry.
attacks.backbone.evidence: A dependency every downstream customer resolves kept answering with an added record after the change was reverted, reinstated from configuration rather than memory.
attacks.https.title: Encrypted web exfiltration
attacks.https.clue: A system repeatedly uploads data to a rarely used web destination.
attacks.https.evidence: Data was uploaded steadily over encrypted web traffic to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
attacks.dnsout.title: DNS covert channel
attacks.dnsout.clue: Name lookups ask for long, repetitive, random-looking web addresses.
attacks.dnsout.evidence: High-entropy DNS queries carry encoded data to an externally controlled domain.
attacks.storage.title: Cloud storage export
attacks.storage.clue: Large reads from cloud storage coincide with a spike in outbound transfers.
attacks.storage.evidence: Bulk reads from cloud storage were exported to an unapproved destination.
attacks.beacon.title: Periodic command beacon
attacks.beacon.clue: Short outbound connections repeat at unusually consistent intervals.
attacks.beacon.evidence: A program calls out to new external infrastructure at regular intervals to collect commands.
attacks.saas.title: SaaS synchronisation abuse
attacks.saas.clue: A staff account's approved file-sync connection suddenly moves far more data than usual.
attacks.saas.evidence: A legitimate integration is being used to export protected records.
attacks.deadrop.title: Public dead-drop channel
attacks.deadrop.clue: Computers keep checking a popular public website in an unusual pattern.
attacks.deadrop.evidence: Commands are being collected from content posted on a public platform.
attacks.tunnel.title: Tunnelled remote console
attacks.tunnel.clue: An encrypted session from outside the organisation is held open under a valid support account.
attacks.tunnel.evidence: An interactive administrative console is carried over an established tunnel.
attacks.webhook.title: Approved webhook relay
attacks.webhook.clue: A cloud integration with a trusted collaboration service began moving data at a new rate.
attacks.webhook.evidence: Data is posted to an integration channel the attacker controls.
attacks.mailout.title: Mailbox export channel
attacks.mailout.clue: A mailbox began forwarding large attachments to an external address.
attacks.mailout.evidence: Protected content is relayed outward through an approved mail path.
attacks.paste.title: Paste-service staging
attacks.paste.clue: A workstation repeatedly retrieves content from a public text service.
attacks.paste.evidence: Commands and exfiltrated data are staged through a public paste site.
attacks.splitzip.title: Split archive upload
attacks.splitzip.clue: Cloud storage received many small file pieces with matching names.
attacks.splitzip.evidence: An archive was split into parts below the alerting size, staged in the organisation's own cloud storage and shared out by public link.
attacks.dns-txt.title: TXT record retrieval
attacks.dns-txt.clue: Name lookups fetch text entries for web domains the business never uses.
attacks.dns-txt.evidence: Data is retrieved from text records on domains the attacker registered for the purpose.
attacks.stream.title: Streaming service relay
attacks.stream.clue: Outbound media traffic exceeds any known service need.
attacks.stream.evidence: Protected content is carried inside an allowed streaming session.
attacks.ssh-out.title: Outbound administrative tunnel
attacks.ssh-out.clue: An internal server now opens administrative sessions to the internet.
attacks.ssh-out.evidence: A reverse administrative tunnel gives interactive access from outside the estate.
attacks.git-out.title: Repository mirror export
attacks.git-out.clue: A repository is being mirrored to an unapproved destination.
attacks.git-out.evidence: Source and configuration are pushed to storage outside the organisation.
attacks.spool.title: Print spooler extraction
attacks.spool.clue: A server began writing documents it was not asked to print.
attacks.spool.evidence: Queued print documents are captured and stored for later removal.
attacks.physical.title: Physical media export
attacks.physical.clue: A computer wrote a large archive to removable media outside business hours.
attacks.physical.evidence: Protected data is copied to portable storage attached to an authorised workstation.
attacks.cdn.title: Content delivery covert channel
attacks.cdn.clue: Requests to a content delivery service carry unusually regular, random-looking values.
attacks.cdn.evidence: Command data is hidden inside cache and content-delivery requests.
attacks.reconsuppress.title: Reconciliation suppression
attacks.reconsuppress.clue: A reconciliation report balances against a ledger that does not.
attacks.reconsuppress.evidence: Reconciliation output was suppressed for selected entries, so the settlement summary reports a balanced position the underlying ledger does not support.
attacks.record-export.title: Public record bulk export
attacks.record-export.clue: A records interface returns far more than a caseworker would ask for.
attacks.record-export.evidence: A records interface served bulk responses far beyond a caseworker's pattern, drawing citizen records across case boundaries in a single sweep.
attacks.telemetry-out.title: Telemetry channel misuse
attacks.telemetry-out.clue: A plant telemetry feed carries more than it reports.
attacks.telemetry-out.evidence: A plant telemetry feed carried payloads larger than its own schema allows, using a path the process network is expected to keep open.
attacks.backup-out.title: Backup replication diversion
attacks.backup-out.clue: A backup job replicates to a destination nobody registered.
attacks.backup-out.evidence: A backup job replicated to a destination that appears in no register, moving whole datasets through a route built to carry exactly that.
attacks.manifest.title: Manifest and berth-plan manipulation
attacks.manifest.clue: A cargo declaration and the berth plan describe different vessels.
attacks.manifest.evidence: Cargo declarations were altered against the berth plan they should match, moving what a container is recorded to hold without moving the container, and the altered declarations were relayed to a party outside the port community.
attacks.beneficiary.title: Beneficiary redirection
attacks.beneficiary.clue: Standing payment instructions change without a corresponding request.
attacks.beneficiary.evidence: Standing beneficiary details were changed without a corresponding customer request, so legitimate instructions settle to an account the customer never nominated.
scenarios.quiet-office.title: The quiet intrusion
scenarios.quiet-office.summary: Two staff report odd behaviour on their computers, and a routine check finds traffic leaving that nobody expected.
scenarios.quiet-office.brief: It is 08:40. Two staff report unusual workstation behaviour, while a routine check shows unexpected outbound traffic. Business applications still operate. Determine how access was gained and what followed.
scenarios.quiet-office.scope: Employee endpoints, identity services, remote access, internal application servers and the company's cloud tenancy. Only simulated evidence is used.
scenarios.quiet-office.timeline: Reports began this morning. The evidence window covers the preceding 24 hours.
scenarios.quiet-office.constraints: Telemetry is incomplete. A failed check settles nothing, and a completed one rules out only what its own source could have seen.
scenarios.quiet-office.impact: Payroll and shared business applications remain available, but confidence in privileged identities is falling.
scenarios.quiet-office.lesson: Could your team connect an endpoint report, an identity event and outbound traffic without treating them as separate incidents?
scenarios.quiet-office.leads.0: Two weak signals overlap: a user complaint and an outbound-traffic anomaly. Neither identifies the entry point.
scenarios.quiet-office.leads.1: Authentication, endpoint and egress timestamps do not align cleanly. Establish which record is causal.
scenarios.quiet-office.leads.2: A staff sign-in came from an unfamiliar place at about the time a familiar-looking program started on one workstation.
scenarios.care-network.title: After the night shift
scenarios.care-network.summary: Clinical services remain live while unfamiliar activity spreads behind the scenes.
scenarios.care-network.brief: At a fictional hospital, overnight staff report a sluggish workstation and unfamiliar remote sessions. Patient-facing services remain available. Investigate without assuming shutdown is the safe first action.
scenarios.care-network.scope: Administrative endpoints, the support gateway, identity services and clinical application servers. Medical devices are outside this attack chain.
scenarios.care-network.timeline: The first anomalies occurred during the night shift. Records cover that shift and the previous working day.
scenarios.care-network.constraints: Clinical continuity matters. Isolation can reduce risk but may interrupt time-sensitive work.
scenarios.care-network.impact: Patient care is continuing. The greatest immediate risk is loss of access to supporting records and scheduling.
scenarios.care-network.lesson: Who would authorise isolation of a system supporting clinical work, and what evidence would they need?
scenarios.care-network.leads.0: A slow endpoint and unfamiliar remote sessions may share a cause, or may be unrelated operational noise.
scenarios.care-network.leads.1: Support accounts cross several services during the night shift. Some of that activity is expected.
scenarios.care-network.leads.2: Overnight, a clinical support queue was switched to manual processing after repeated timeouts.
scenarios.power-support.title: Beyond the gateway
scenarios.power-support.summary: A supplier session raises questions at the boundary of plant support systems.
scenarios.power-support.brief: A fictional power operator sees an unusual supplier session to its maintenance environment. A support server later makes unfamiliar connections. Generation remains stable. Reconstruct the support-system compromise.
scenarios.power-support.scope: Supplier remote access, the maintenance jump host, identity services and support servers. Controllers and safety systems are not in scope.
scenarios.power-support.timeline: The suspicious session started after the approved maintenance window. Review the next twelve hours.
scenarios.power-support.constraints: Investigation is read-only. Distinguish a support-system breach from a process-safety event.
scenarios.power-support.impact: Generation is stable, but support access cannot yet be trusted. A rushed shutdown could introduce its own operational risk.
scenarios.power-support.lesson: Could you revoke supplier access without losing essential operational support, and who owns that decision?
scenarios.power-support.leads.0: A supplier session and server traffic are correlated in time, but not yet proven to share an identity.
scenarios.power-support.leads.1: The support environment has legitimate remote administration that can resemble lateral movement.
scenarios.power-support.leads.2: Boundary records are strong; host telemetry on the jump server has gaps.
scenarios.port-terminal.title: A terminal under watch
scenarios.port-terminal.summary: A booking portal anomaly arrives during a busy operating window.
scenarios.port-terminal.brief: A fictional container terminal reports unusual requests to its booking portal. Support staff then spot unexplained server activity. Vessel operations continue. Establish the attack chain before the terminal's schedule runs out.
scenarios.port-terminal.scope: The booking portal, application servers, identity services and business network. Crane control systems are excluded.
scenarios.port-terminal.timeline: Portal anomalies began at 05:30, followed by internal activity during the morning shift.
scenarios.port-terminal.constraints: Busy operations hide suspicious traffic. Preserve evidence before disruptive changes.
scenarios.port-terminal.impact: Bookings continue, but partner data and vessel schedules may be exposed if the portal is not trustworthy.
scenarios.port-terminal.lesson: Which partners need early warning if an operational dependency can no longer be trusted?
scenarios.port-terminal.leads.0: A burst of portal requests could be partner traffic, automated abuse or exploitation.
scenarios.port-terminal.leads.1: Server activity follows the anomaly, but the available logs cannot yet prove direction of travel.
scenarios.port-terminal.leads.2: Partner identities and public application traffic overlap in the same time window.
scenarios.cloud-control.title: An identity out of place
scenarios.cloud-control.summary: An automation account begins acting beyond its normal workload.
scenarios.cloud-control.brief: A fictional cloud provider detects unusual control-plane activity and an egress-cost spike. No scheduled deployment explains either. Investigate the identity, permission path and mechanism maintaining access.
scenarios.cloud-control.scope: Workload credentials, access management, control-plane logs and object-storage activity. No real cloud account is connected.
scenarios.cloud-control.timeline: The anomaly began several hours after the last approved deployment.
scenarios.cloud-control.constraints: Successful API calls can still be malicious. Attribute the caller before assuming the credential’s owner acted.
scenarios.cloud-control.impact: Customer workloads are online. Unchecked privilege expansion could expose multiple tenants and increase transfer costs.
scenarios.cloud-control.lesson: Could you rotate a compromised workload credential safely and identify every role and key derived from it?
scenarios.cloud-control.leads.0: Valid API calls and higher transfer volume are the only confirmed facts.
scenarios.cloud-control.leads.1: The credential owner, execution location and assumed role may be three different things.
scenarios.cloud-control.leads.2: A role's permissions were widened yesterday, and nobody has yet matched the change to a deployment.
scenarios.shared-services.title: A trusted connection
scenarios.shared-services.summary: A shared-service identity links an isolated alert to a wider incident.
scenarios.shared-services.brief: A fictional shared-services operator sees an unfamiliar session under a trusted support identity. A dependent application later reports unexpected access. Service remains available, but scope is unclear.
scenarios.shared-services.scope: Remote support, identity services, shared application servers, the shared cloud platform and outbound records. Connected organisations are not directly accessible.
scenarios.shared-services.timeline: Anomalies cluster around the last support window. Begin with the shared service’s own evidence.
scenarios.shared-services.constraints: Do not assume trust extends across every connected service. Separate confirmed evidence from partner reports.
scenarios.shared-services.impact: Dependent organisations still receive service, but each additional minute increases the chance of propagating bad trust decisions.
scenarios.shared-services.lesson: What evidence can you share promptly, and how will you separate confirmed facts from assumptions?
scenarios.shared-services.leads.0: A trusted identity appears in two environments, but only one side has complete telemetry.
scenarios.shared-services.leads.1: The dependent application report may reveal scope, or may be a separate incident.
scenarios.shared-services.leads.2: An administrator from the shared-services side signed in to a tenant system at an hour nobody normally works.
scenarios.government-service.title: Authority under pressure
scenarios.government-service.summary: A privileged administrative identity appears across citizen-service systems.
scenarios.government-service.brief: A fictional government digital service detects anomalous privileged access shortly before a high-demand public transaction window. Services remain available, but the trust boundary is uncertain.
scenarios.government-service.scope: Administrative identities, citizen-service applications, shared hosting and outbound telemetry.
scenarios.government-service.timeline: The first privileged event occurred ninety minutes before the demand surge.
scenarios.government-service.constraints: Public access must be preserved where safe. Attribution is incomplete and multiple agencies depend on the platform.
scenarios.government-service.impact: A loss of trust could delay essential public transactions and trigger cross-agency coordination.
scenarios.government-service.lesson: How quickly can confirmed facts be shared without overstating scope?
scenarios.government-service.leads.0: A privileged action is confirmed, but the initiating identity may have been replayed.
scenarios.government-service.leads.1: Application and identity logs disagree on the apparent source.
scenarios.government-service.leads.2: A shared administrative path may connect otherwise separate services.
scenarios.telecom-core.title: Signals in the core
scenarios.telecom-core.summary: Management-plane activity overlaps with an emerging service-quality issue.
scenarios.telecom-core.brief: A fictional telecommunications provider observes unusual management access while customers report intermittent service degradation. Determine whether the events form one incident.
scenarios.telecom-core.scope: Management identities, support systems, network-management servers, the cloud-hosted provisioning platform and egress records. Live customer traffic content is excluded.
scenarios.telecom-core.timeline: The access anomaly preceded service reports by forty minutes.
scenarios.telecom-core.constraints: Containment must avoid unnecessary loss of national connectivity.
scenarios.telecom-core.impact: Service remains broadly available, but further degradation could affect dependent essential services.
scenarios.telecom-core.lesson: Which control-plane actions require immediate joint cyber and operations authority?
scenarios.telecom-core.leads.0: A valid support session accessed an uncommon management path.
scenarios.telecom-core.leads.1: Service degradation may be operational noise or an attacker consequence.
scenarios.telecom-core.leads.2: Several management changes were logged under maintenance tickets nobody remembers raising.
scenarios.water-operations.title: Pressure boundary
scenarios.water-operations.summary: A support-system anomaly emerges while treatment operations remain stable.
scenarios.water-operations.brief: A fictional water operator identifies an unapproved remote session and configuration access in an engineering support environment. Treatment remains within safe operating limits.
scenarios.water-operations.scope: Remote support, engineering workstations, historian support and identity services. Process controllers remain read-only in this exercise.
scenarios.water-operations.timeline: The session began after a vendor maintenance task was closed.
scenarios.water-operations.constraints: Cyber actions must preserve safe and continuous water operations.
scenarios.water-operations.impact: Operations are stable, but engineering trust and future maintenance confidence are degrading.
scenarios.water-operations.lesson: Can the team distinguish compromise of engineering support from a process-safety event?
scenarios.water-operations.leads.0: Vendor access remained active beyond its approved window.
scenarios.water-operations.leads.1: A support workstation and historian show related but incomplete evidence.
scenarios.water-operations.leads.2: The historian shows readings requested at hours when no operator was on shift.
scenarios.financial-clearing.title: The clearing window
scenarios.financial-clearing.summary: An identity anomaly appears before a time-sensitive settlement cycle.
scenarios.financial-clearing.brief: A fictional financial institution detects unusual privileged activity and an unexpected export pattern before settlement processing. Determine the route without disrupting trusted transactions unnecessarily.
scenarios.financial-clearing.scope: Privileged identities, payment-support applications, cloud workloads and outbound transfer records.
scenarios.financial-clearing.timeline: Activity began two hours before the next settlement cycle.
scenarios.financial-clearing.constraints: Integrity and availability matter equally. Decisions must be defensible under tight time pressure.
scenarios.financial-clearing.impact: Transactions continue, but data integrity and settlement confidence could deteriorate rapidly.
scenarios.financial-clearing.lesson: What evidence is sufficient to constrain access before a critical financial window?
scenarios.financial-clearing.leads.0: A valid privileged identity initiated unusual but permitted activity.
scenarios.financial-clearing.leads.1: The export pattern may be reconciliation traffic or staged data.
scenarios.financial-clearing.leads.2: Two reconciliation reports for the same window disagree by a small amount.
difficulties.training.title: Training
difficulties.training.description: More time and a clearer margin to learn in; the score allows six turns before a slower finish costs anything.
difficulties.operational.title: Operational
difficulties.crisis.title: Crisis
difficulties.crisis.description: Tighter rolls, fewer turns and higher starting impact.
hypotheses.identity.title: Identity-led intrusion
hypotheses.identity.premise: A real account, sign-in or granted permission is being misused — to get in, to move around and to take data out.
hypotheses.endpoint.title: Compromised host
hypotheses.endpoint.premise: Malicious software on a computer or server is doing the work, from the first program it runs, even one that arrived in a trusted update, to whatever it sends out.
hypotheses.application.title: Application or supplier path
hypotheses.application.premise: A public-facing application, a supplier's delivery channel or the open internet is doing the work — an exposed service or a vendor push on the way in, web, hosting or DNS traffic on the way out.
hypotheses.cloud.title: Cloud control-plane abuse
hypotheses.cloud.premise: Cloud keys, roles and settings are being used beyond what they were set up for — in the cloud account's own management, storage and connected services.
sectorProcedures.change-review.title: Change and approval review
sectorProcedures.change-review.short: Privileged change records against what changed
sectorProcedures.change-review.descripti: Reconcile the privileged change record with the changes systems actually received.
sectorProcedures.change-review.question: Was every change that landed also requested and approved?
sectorProcedures.downtime-check.title: Downtime dependency check
sectorProcedures.downtime-check.descript: Validate that clinical downtime procedures still work and which access paths they depend on.
sectorProcedures.downtime-check.question: If this path is cut, can care continue on the fallback?
sectorProcedures.work-order.title: Work order validation
sectorProcedures.work-order.short: The maintenance permit against the route used
sectorProcedures.work-order.description: Check the maintenance work order against the access route the session actually took.
sectorProcedures.work-order.question: Was this maintenance authorised, and did it arrive the way it should have?
sectorProcedures.manifest-recon.title: Manifest and berth reconciliation
sectorProcedures.manifest-recon.short: Cargo declarations against the berth plan
sectorProcedures.manifest-recon.descript: Reconcile cargo declarations, manifests and the berth plan against the moves the terminal recorded.
sectorProcedures.manifest-recon.question: Do the paperwork and the yard describe the same vessel?
sectorProcedures.plane-replay.title: Control-plane change reconstruction
sectorProcedures.plane-replay.short: Role and key changes in sequence
sectorProcedures.plane-replay.descriptio: Reconstruct control-plane changes in order, across regions and tenants.
sectorProcedures.plane-replay.question: In what order were these roles and keys changed, and by which identity?
sectorProcedures.propagation.title: Downstream propagation trace
sectorProcedures.propagation.description: Trace what the shared platform pushed downstream and which customers received it.
sectorProcedures.propagation.question: How far past our own estate did this reach?
sectorProcedures.federation-review.title: Cross-agency federation review
sectorProcedures.federation-review.short: Sign-ins one department vouches for to another
sectorProcedures.federation-review.descr: Review identity assertions crossing agency boundaries and the trust that accepted them.
sectorProcedures.federation-review.quest: Which department vouched for this, and on what basis?
sectorProcedures.route-compare.title: Routing change comparison
sectorProcedures.route-compare.short: Live routing against the approved plan
sectorProcedures.route-compare.descripti: Compare live routing and management-plane state with the approved network plan.
sectorProcedures.route-compare.question: Does the network match the plan it was supposed to be built to?
sectorProcedures.historian-recon.title: Historian reconciliation
sectorProcedures.historian-recon.descrip: Reconcile historian records against the process state operators observed at the time.
sectorProcedures.historian-recon.questio: Does the record agree with what the plant was actually doing?
sectorProcedures.settlement-recon.title: Approval and settlement reconstruction
sectorProcedures.settlement-recon.short: The approval chain behind each instruction
sectorProcedures.settlement-recon.descri: Reconstruct the approval sequence behind settled instructions, including who signed and when.
sectorProcedures.settlement-recon.questi: Who approved this, in what order, and does the ledger agree?
scenarioDynamics.0.label: Business service integrity
scenarioDynamics.0.objective: Exploit trusted identities and quietly reach shared business data.
scenarioDynamics.0.reaction: The actor rotates to another trusted session after detecting intervention.
scenarioDynamics.0.escalations.0: A privileged session begins accessing an additional business service.
scenarioDynamics.0.escalations.1: Payroll data is staged on an internal share.
scenarioDynamics.0.escalations.2: A second administrator account shows anomalous activity.
scenarioDynamics.0.countermeasure: Earlier identity revocation would have reduced spread, but risked locking out legitimate administrators.
scenarioDynamics.1.label: Clinical service continuity
scenarioDynamics.1.objective: Use support access to reach administrative records without triggering a clinical outage.
scenarioDynamics.1.reaction: The actor shifts activity into a different support account and reduces its request rate.
scenarioDynamics.1.escalations.0: The scheduling service begins responding slowly.
scenarioDynamics.1.escalations.1: A clinical support queue moves to manual processing.
scenarioDynamics.1.escalations.2: Staff report intermittent access to administrative records.
scenarioDynamics.1.countermeasure: A segmented support path would have limited movement while preserving most clinical activity.
scenarioDynamics.2.label: Trusted maintenance access
scenarioDynamics.2.objective: Remain inside the support environment and abuse legitimate maintenance pathways.
scenarioDynamics.2.reaction: The actor abandons the observed session and moves toward a dormant supplier trust path.
scenarioDynamics.2.escalations.0: A maintenance job is delayed while access is verified.
scenarioDynamics.2.escalations.1: The jump host can no longer be treated as a trusted administration point.
scenarioDynamics.2.escalations.2: Operations invokes an alternate maintenance process.
scenarioDynamics.2.countermeasure: Revoking all supplier access earlier would have reduced cyber risk but weakened operational support.
scenarioDynamics.3.label: Terminal service flow
scenarioDynamics.3.objective: Use the booking environment to obtain partner data and disrupt trusted transactions.
scenarioDynamics.3.reaction: The actor changes infrastructure and begins blending with partner-originated traffic.
scenarioDynamics.3.escalations.1: A vessel schedule update enters a manual review queue.
scenarioDynamics.3.escalations.2: The terminal activates a continuity process for partner transactions.
scenarioDynamics.3.countermeasure: Earlier portal isolation would have constrained access but caused a larger partner-service interruption.
scenarioDynamics.4.label: Platform availability
scenarioDynamics.4.objective: Expand control-plane privileges and export data through legitimate cloud services.
scenarioDynamics.4.reaction: The actor exchanges the observed credential for another role and changes the export path.
scenarioDynamics.4.escalations.0: A second tenant boundary requires urgent review.
scenarioDynamics.4.escalations.1: Unplanned egress cost continues to rise.
scenarioDynamics.4.escalations.2: The provider restricts one automation workflow pending validation.
scenarioDynamics.4.countermeasure: Broad credential rotation would have reduced attacker options but disrupted dependent automation.
scenarioDynamics.5.label: Downstream trust
scenarioDynamics.5.objective: Propagate through shared identities before dependent organisations can coordinate.
scenarioDynamics.5.reaction: The actor lowers activity on the shared service and tests a downstream trust relationship.
scenarioDynamics.5.escalations.0: A dependent organisation requests urgent indicators.
scenarioDynamics.5.escalations.1: Another connected service suspends automated trust.
scenarioDynamics.5.escalations.2: Coordination delays leave one downstream environment without confirmed scope.
scenarioDynamics.5.countermeasure: Earlier partner notification could have reduced downstream exposure, while sharing less-certain information.
scenarioDynamics.6.label: Public service integrity
scenarioDynamics.6.objective: Exploit privileged trust to reach multiple citizen-service applications.
scenarioDynamics.6.reaction: The actor shifts into a shared administrative identity and lowers its activity rate.
scenarioDynamics.6.escalations.0: A second public service reports anomalous administration.
scenarioDynamics.6.escalations.2: Cross-agency coordination moves to crisis posture.
scenarioDynamics.6.countermeasure: Earlier privilege restriction could have reduced spread but delayed legitimate public-service administration.
scenarioDynamics.7.label: Connectivity continuity
scenarioDynamics.7.objective: Abuse management access while blending with legitimate operational change.
scenarioDynamics.7.reaction: The actor rotates to a dormant support path and changes its management endpoint.
scenarioDynamics.7.escalations.0: Service degradation expands to another region.
scenarioDynamics.7.escalations.1: A dependent operator requests urgent assurance.
scenarioDynamics.7.countermeasure: Earlier segmentation of management access could have constrained the actor with less customer disruption.
scenarioDynamics.8.label: Treatment continuity
scenarioDynamics.8.objective: Preserve access to engineering support while approaching operational dependencies.
scenarioDynamics.8.reaction: The actor abandons the observed session and tests an older vendor credential.
scenarioDynamics.8.escalations.2: Operations increases monitoring of treatment tolerances.
scenarioDynamics.8.countermeasure: Earlier vendor-session revocation would have reduced risk while requiring an alternate maintenance process.
scenarioDynamics.9.label: Settlement integrity
scenarioDynamics.9.objective: Use privileged and cloud access to alter or export sensitive transaction data.
scenarioDynamics.9.reaction: The actor exchanges the observed role for another trusted application path.
scenarioDynamics.9.escalations.2: A critical processing window approaches with unresolved scope.
scenarioDynamics.9.countermeasure: Earlier credential restriction could have reduced exposure while slowing legitimate settlement preparation.
gameModes.campaign.title: Campaign
gameModes.campaign.description: Persistent readiness, trust and team fatigue carry between incidents.
gameModes.daily.title: Daily operation
gameModes.daily.description: A fixed incident seed gives every commander the same case today.
gameModes.weekly.title: Weekly operation
gameModes.weekly.description: One case and seed at Operational for the whole week, so a week's commanders can compare results by its code.
gameModes.ironman.title: Ironman
gameModes.ironman.description: No mid-incident save and one fewer turn. Decisions are final.
gameModes.escalation.title: Escalation
gameModes.escalation.description: Begin under pressure against an actor already moving.
gameModes.expert.title: Expert
gameModes.expert.description: No coaching or suggested evidence, and every roll is one harder (−1).
specialists.hunter.title: Threat hunter
specialists.hunter.ability: +1 when using hunting, network or intelligence evidence.
specialists.forensics.title: Forensics lead
specialists.forensics.ability: +1 when using endpoint, server or forensic evidence.
specialists.identity.title: Identity specialist
specialists.identity.ability: +1 when using identity, cloud or email evidence.
specialists.ot.title: OT security engineer
specialists.ot.ability: +1 on boundary evidence and reduces sector degradation.
specialists.continuity.title: Continuity lead
specialists.continuity.ability: Reduces continuity and sector-health losses from investigative delay.
specialists.communications.title: Communications lead
specialists.communications.ability: Reduces business pressure and improves leadership decisions.
procedureScopes.focused.title: Focused
procedureScopes.focused.description: Test the working hypothesis against the most relevant system.
procedureScopes.enterprise.title: Enterprise
procedureScopes.enterprise.description: Search connected environments for broader scope at a time cost.
procedureIntensities.rapid.title: Rapid
procedureIntensities.rapid.description: Move quickly with lower analytical confidence.
procedureIntensities.balanced.title: Balanced
procedureIntensities.balanced.descriptio: Balance confidence, time and operational pressure.
procedureIntensities.exhaustive.title: Exhaustive
procedureIntensities.exhaustive.descript: Increase confidence, but consume time and specialist capacity.
adversaryObjectives.exfiltration.title: Strategic data theft
adversaryObjectives.exfiltration.tell: The actor is staging and moving high-value information.
adversaryObjectives.exfiltration.outboun: The outbound stage is the objective itself: the channel carries the collected material out, and its volume and timing are the measure of what was lost.
adversaryObjectives.fraud.title: Financial manipulation
adversaryObjectives.fraud.tell: The actor is seeking trusted transactions and approval paths.
adversaryObjectives.fraud.outbound: The outbound stage carries approval patterns, counterparty detail and timing out, and carries instructions back in, so the manipulation can be made to look routine.
adversaryObjectives.espionage.title: Long-term collection
adversaryObjectives.espionage.tell: The actor values durable access and low-noise collection.
adversaryObjectives.espionage.outbound: The outbound stage is the collection pipeline: low and slow by design, sized to stay under the thresholds that would expose it.
adversaryObjectives.preposition.title: Strategic pre-positioning
adversaryObjectives.preposition.tell: The actor is mapping dependencies for later operational effect.
adversaryObjectives.preposition.outbound: The outbound stage is reconnaissance leaving, not value: dependency maps, contact paths and operating schedules that make a later effect precise. Its modest volume is the point, not a reassurance.
sectorSystems.0.title: Business confidence margin
sectorSystems.0.rule: Identity and cloud exposure erodes business confidence fastest; monitoring restores a little, while isolating a control path adds administrative cost.
sectorSystems.0.plain: How far the business still trusts its shared IT services: sign-in, email and the applications staff rely on.
sectorSystems.0.transmissions.0: Payroll owners request a confidence assessment.
sectorSystems.0.transmissions.1: Privileged access owners begin an emergency review.
sectorSystems.1.title: Clinical service margin
sectorSystems.1.rule: Containment cuts deepest here: every isolation costs clinical margin, failed analysis costs more, and exhaustive analysis taxes continuity.
sectorSystems.1.plain: How much room the hospital has left to keep treating patients safely while systems are disrupted.
sectorSystems.1.transmissions.0: Clinical operations asks whether scheduling can remain online.
sectorSystems.1.transmissions.1: The duty manager reports growing workstation delays.
sectorSystems.2.title: Operational support integrity
sectorSystems.2.rule: Successful boundary investigation protects support integrity and monitoring recovers it fastest, but any isolation erodes engineering support.
sectorSystems.2.plain: Whether the engineers who support the plant's control systems can still do so safely.
sectorSystems.2.transmissions.0: Plant operations confirms generation remains stable.
sectorSystems.2.transmissions.1: The supplier cannot validate the remote session.
sectorSystems.3.title: Terminal schedule margin
sectorSystems.3.rule: The schedule margin runs down quickly: adversary tempo counts double and capacity falls faster from the fourth turn onward.
sectorSystems.3.plain: How much of the port's working window is left to move cargo before vessels are delayed.
sectorSystems.3.transmissions.0: Vessel planners ask whether partner bookings remain trusted.
sectorSystems.3.transmissions.1: The terminal approaches its next operating cut-off.
sectorSystems.4.title: Tenant trust boundary
sectorSystems.4.rule: Control-plane and identity exposure widens tenant risk fastest; enterprise-scope hunting advances the attacker objective and monitoring reassures little.
sectorSystems.4.plain: How confident the customers who share the cloud platform can be that they are kept apart from one another.
sectorSystems.4.transmissions.0: A second tenant reports an unusual control-plane event.
sectorSystems.4.transmissions.1: Transfer volume continues to rise without a deployment record.
sectorSystems.5.title: Shared-service confidence
sectorSystems.5.rule: Unverified trust propagates to dependent organisations: failed analysis costs the most confidence, and a focus too narrow for the shared path loses more.
sectorSystems.5.plain: How far the organisations that depend on this shared service still trust it.
sectorSystems.5.transmissions.0: A dependent organisation requests confirmed indicators.
sectorSystems.5.transmissions.1: Shared support teams report conflicting identity records.
sectorSystems.6.title: Public transaction capacity
sectorSystems.6.rule: Public demand constrains disruptive containment: a communications lead protects capacity, while isolation is more disruptive than usual.
sectorSystems.6.plain: How much of the public service people can still use to complete their transactions.
sectorSystems.6.transmissions.0: The public transaction peak begins in forty minutes.
sectorSystems.6.transmissions.1: Two agencies request a common operating picture.
sectorSystems.7.title: Core network stability
sectorSystems.7.rule: Core stability decays fastest of all sectors, but successful network, firewall or DNS analysis restores it quickly.
sectorSystems.7.plain: How stable the core network is for the customers whose calls and data cross it.
sectorSystems.7.transmissions.0: Network operations sees instability in a neighbouring domain.
sectorSystems.8.title: Process safety margin
sectorSystems.8.rule: The safety margin is the most resilient to delay, but enterprise-scope actions and any isolation erode it sharply.
sectorSystems.8.plain: How much safety margin the treatment process has before water quality is put at risk.
sectorSystems.8.transmissions.0: Operators move one process area to manual supervision.
sectorSystems.8.transmissions.1: Engineering requests confirmation that safety logic is unaffected.
sectorSystems.9.title: Clearing-window integrity
sectorSystems.9.rule: Integrity erodes with delay and failure: adversary tempo counts double and every failed procedure costs more close to settlement.
sectorSystems.9.plain: Whether payments can still be settled correctly before the clearing window closes.
sectorSystems.9.transmissions.0: Fraud operations identifies several unusual approvals.
infrastructureTopologies.0.title: Enterprise trust map
infrastructureTopologies.0.criticalRule: The shared application platform supports every dependent workflow, so isolating it carries the highest service cost.
infrastructureTopologies.1.title: Clinical support map
infrastructureTopologies.1.criticalRule: The records store sets the clinical-continuity cost of containment, so it is the critical dependency.
infrastructureTopologies.2.title: Generation support map
infrastructureTopologies.2.criticalRule: The engineering zone holds operational authority, so it is critical and isolating it needs plant approval.
infrastructureTopologies.3.title: Terminal dependency map
infrastructureTopologies.3.criticalRule: The booking portal is the partner-facing edge, so it is critical and isolating it severs external transactions first.
infrastructureTopologies.4.title: Cloud trust map
infrastructureTopologies.4.criticalRule: Control-plane isolation removes the privilege path that reaches every tenant resource, so it is critical.
infrastructureTopologies.5.title: Shared-service map
infrastructureTopologies.5.criticalRule: The shared gateway is the single trust entry point, so it is critical and isolating it affects every connected organisation.
infrastructureTopologies.6.title: Public-service map
infrastructureTopologies.6.criticalRule: Transaction records carry legal and public-accountability weight, so they are critical and their isolation is the costliest decision.
infrastructureTopologies.7.title: Core network map
infrastructureTopologies.7.criticalRule: The network core carries national traffic, so it is critical and isolating it is the highest-consequence action on this map.
infrastructureTopologies.8.title: Water support map
infrastructureTopologies.8.criticalRule: Process supervision carries safety authority, so it is critical and isolating it requires operations approval.
infrastructureTopologies.9.title: Clearing trust map
infrastructureTopologies.9.criticalRule: Settlement records underpin transaction finality, so they are critical and their isolation halts completion.

sectorSetPieces.sector-0.title: Privileged reset window
sectorSetPieces.sector-0.prompt: Business owners can support one coordinated identity reset before payroll processing begins.
sectorSetPieces.sector-0.a.title: Reset the privileged tier
sectorSetPieces.sector-0.a.detail: Reduce identity risk while accepting a short administrative freeze.
sectorSetPieces.sector-0.b.title: Protect payroll availability
sectorSetPieces.sector-0.b.detail: Delay the reset and monitor privileged sessions through processing.
sectorSetPieces.sector-0.c.title: Reset only the exposed accounts

sectorSetPieces.sector-2.title: Supplier support boundary
sectorSetPieces.sector-2.prompt: Plant operations can suspend remote maintenance or preserve vendor support through the shift.
sectorSetPieces.sector-2.a.title: Suspend supplier access
sectorSetPieces.sector-2.a.detail: Protect the boundary while local engineers assume support duties.
sectorSetPieces.sector-2.b.title: Maintain supervised access
sectorSetPieces.sector-2.b.detail: Retain support capacity while monitoring the supplier session.
sectorSetPieces.sector-2.c.title: Reduce supplier access to read-only
sectorSetPieces.sector-2.c.detail: The vendor keeps diagnostics and loses the ability to change anything.
sectorSetPieces.sector-3.title: Vessel-planning cut-off
sectorSetPieces.sector-3.prompt: The next operating plan must be issued before the terminal can fully validate the booking platform.
sectorSetPieces.sector-3.a.title: Issue a manual validated plan
sectorSetPieces.sector-3.a.detail: Slow terminal flow to avoid propagating untrusted data.
sectorSetPieces.sector-3.b.title: Continue automated planning
sectorSetPieces.sector-3.b.detail: Protect capacity but rely on a platform under investigation.
sectorSetPieces.sector-3.c.title: Validate partner-originated bookings only
sectorSetPieces.sector-3.c.detail: Automated planning continues for internal traffic while partner entries are checked by hand.
sectorSetPieces.sector-4.title: Tenant isolation boundary
sectorSetPieces.sector-4.prompt: A potentially affected tenant can be isolated, but shared control-plane evidence is incomplete.
sectorSetPieces.sector-4.a.title: Isolate the affected tenant
sectorSetPieces.sector-4.a.detail: Constrain exposure while accepting customer disruption.
sectorSetPieces.sector-4.b.title: Constrain privileges only
sectorSetPieces.sector-4.b.detail: Preserve workload access with more residual uncertainty.
sectorSetPieces.sector-4.c.title: Isolate the affected workload only
sectorSetPieces.sector-4.c.detail: Constrain the one workload the evidence reaches rather than the whole tenant.
sectorSetPieces.sector-5.title: Partner warning threshold
sectorSetPieces.sector-5.prompt: Dependent organisations need to know whether the trusted support identity remains safe.
sectorSetPieces.sector-5.a.title: Issue a qualified warning
sectorSetPieces.sector-5.a.detail: Share confirmed facts and uncertainty so partners can protect themselves.
sectorSetPieces.sector-5.b.title: Wait for attribution
sectorSetPieces.sector-5.b.detail: Avoid unnecessary alarm but delay partner action.
sectorSetPieces.sector-5.c.title: Notify the affected partners privately
sectorSetPieces.sector-5.c.detail: Tell the organisations the evidence actually touches, with what is known and what is not.
sectorSetPieces.sector-6.title: Public transaction surge
sectorSetPieces.sector-6.prompt: A demand peak has begun while the administrative trust boundary remains uncertain.
sectorSetPieces.sector-6.a.title: Restrict administration
sectorSetPieces.sector-6.a.detail: Freeze privileged change while keeping public transactions available.
sectorSetPieces.sector-6.b.title: Maintain normal administration
sectorSetPieces.sector-6.b.detail: Preserve operational flexibility while the trust path remains exposed.
sectorSetPieces.sector-6.c.title: Require a second approver for privileged change
sectorSetPieces.sector-6.c.detail: Administration continues under dual control, slower but accountable.
sectorSetPieces.sector-7.title: Core routing instability
sectorSetPieces.sector-7.prompt: A neighbouring network domain is unstable and may be connected to the intrusion.
sectorSetPieces.sector-7.a.title: Quarantine the management route
sectorSetPieces.sector-7.a.detail: Constrain movement with a controlled subscriber impact.
sectorSetPieces.sector-7.b.title: Observe routing behaviour
sectorSetPieces.sector-7.b.detail: Preserve visibility while accepting cascading network risk.
sectorSetPieces.sector-7.c.title: Pin the affected prefixes to a known-good policy
sectorSetPieces.sector-7.c.detail: Hold the narrow route range steady without quarantining the management plane.
sectorSetPieces.sector-8.title: Manual process operation
sectorSetPieces.sector-8.prompt: Operators can move one process area to manual supervision before support access is constrained.
sectorSetPieces.sector-8.a.title: Enter manual supervision
sectorSetPieces.sector-8.a.detail: Create a safer cyber-response window at an operating cost.
sectorSetPieces.sector-8.b.title: Remain in normal control
sectorSetPieces.sector-8.b.detail: Preserve efficiency but narrow the margin for cyber intervention.
sectorSetPieces.sector-8.c.title: Put one process area under closer supervision
sectorSetPieces.sector-8.c.detail: An operator watches the affected area directly while the rest of the plant runs as normal.
sectorSetPieces.sector-9.title: Clearing cut-off
sectorSetPieces.sector-9.prompt: Several unusual approvals must be accepted, delayed or rejected before settlement.
sectorSetPieces.sector-9.a.title: Hold high-risk transactions
sectorSetPieces.sector-9.a.detail: Protect clearing integrity while legitimate settlement is reviewed.
sectorSetPieces.sector-9.b.title: Clear and investigate later
sectorSetPieces.sector-9.b.detail: Meet the deadline while accepting possible fraudulent settlement.
sectorSetPieces.sector-9.c.title: Require out-of-band approval above a lowered threshold
sectorSetPieces.sector-9.c.detail: Settlement continues, with anything above a reduced limit confirmed on a second channel.
secondSetPieces.sector-0-b.title: Board pack mail run
secondSetPieces.sector-0-b.prompt: The mail team can hold every external message for scanning before the board pack goes out tonight.
secondSetPieces.sector-0-b.a.title: Hold all external mail for scanning
secondSetPieces.sector-0-b.a.detail: Every outside message waits for the scanner, and the board pack goes out late.
secondSetPieces.sector-0-b.b.title: Keep mail flowing
secondSetPieces.sector-0-b.b.detail: Deliver as normal and review the mail logs afterwards.
secondSetPieces.sector-0-b.c.title: Hold mail to finance and executives only
secondSetPieces.sector-0-b.c.detail: The people the evidence points at wait for scanning; everyone else receives mail as normal.
secondSetPieces.sector-1-b.title: Medication cabinet link
secondSetPieces.sector-1-b.prompt: The ward medication cabinets sync with a system the intruder may have touched. Night rounds start within the hour.
secondSetPieces.sector-1-b.a.title: Run the cabinets offline
secondSetPieces.sector-1-b.a.detail: Nurses dispense from local records and paper charts until the link is checked.
secondSetPieces.sector-1-b.b.title: Keep the cabinets synced
secondSetPieces.sector-1-b.b.detail: Rounds run normally while the link carries whatever it carries.
secondSetPieces.sector-1-b.c.title: Pharmacist check on controlled drugs
secondSetPieces.sector-1-b.c.detail: The link stays up, and a pharmacist confirms every controlled-drug release by phone.
secondSetPieces.sector-2-b.title: Plant data export
secondSetPieces.sector-2-b.prompt: Plant data leaves for the corporate network every fifteen minutes, across the boundary under investigation.
secondSetPieces.sector-2-b.a.title: Stop the export
secondSetPieces.sector-2-b.a.detail: Corporate reports go blind while the boundary is checked; operators still see the plant.
secondSetPieces.sector-2-b.b.title: Keep exporting
secondSetPieces.sector-2-b.b.detail: Trading and planning keep their numbers, and the path stays open.
secondSetPieces.sector-2-b.c.title: Send it through a one-way gateway
secondSetPieces.sector-2-b.c.detail: Data still leaves the plant, and nothing can come back along the same path.
secondSetPieces.sector-3-b.title: Crane software update
secondSetPieces.sector-3-b.prompt: The crane supplier wants to push a scheduled update tonight through its remote channel.
secondSetPieces.sector-3-b.a.title: Close the channel and postpone
secondSetPieces.sector-3-b.a.detail: No remote changes to the cranes until the channel is cleared; a known fault stays unfixed.
secondSetPieces.sector-3-b.b.title: Let the update run
secondSetPieces.sector-3-b.b.detail: The cranes get their fix through a channel nobody has cleared.
secondSetPieces.sector-3-b.c.title: Install it on site, one crane first
secondSetPieces.sector-3-b.c.detail: An engineer brings the update in person on checked media and installs it on one crane before the rest.
secondSetPieces.sector-4-b.title: Customer key rotation
secondSetPieces.sector-4-b.prompt: Customers ask whether to change their access keys. Forcing it breaks every integration that has not been updated.
secondSetPieces.sector-4-b.a.title: Force new keys for every customer
secondSetPieces.sector-4-b.a.detail: All keys change tonight; integrations break until customers update them.
secondSetPieces.sector-4-b.b.title: Advise, enforce nothing
secondSetPieces.sector-4-b.b.detail: Customers choose, and most will wait.
secondSetPieces.sector-4-b.c.title: Force new keys where use looks unusual
secondSetPieces.sector-4-b.c.detail: Only keys signed in from outside their normal pattern change; the rest are left to their owners.
secondSetPieces.sector-5-b.title: Shared certificate
secondSetPieces.sector-5-b.prompt: The intruder may hold a copy of a certificate many customers trust. Replacing it means every client must load the new one.
secondSetPieces.sector-5-b.a.title: Revoke and replace it now
secondSetPieces.sector-5-b.a.detail: The old certificate stops working tonight, along with every client that has not updated.
secondSetPieces.sector-5-b.b.title: Keep the current certificate
secondSetPieces.sector-5-b.b.detail: Nothing breaks, and a possibly copied certificate stays trusted.
secondSetPieces.sector-5-b.c.title: Replace it with a day's overlap
secondSetPieces.sector-5-b.c.detail: Both certificates work for a day while clients move over, and the old one is watched closely.
secondSetPieces.sector-6-b.title: Weekly payment run
secondSetPieces.sector-6-b.prompt: The weekly benefit payment run is due, and the case system that feeds it is under investigation.
secondSetPieces.sector-6-b.a.title: Delay the payment run
secondSetPieces.sector-6-b.a.detail: No payments go until the records are checked, and claimants wait.
secondSetPieces.sector-6-b.b.title: Pay as normal
secondSetPieces.sector-6-b.b.detail: Claimants are paid on time from records nobody has checked.
secondSetPieces.sector-6-b.c.title: Pay, holding recently changed accounts
secondSetPieces.sector-6-b.c.detail: Most payments go on time; accounts whose bank details changed this week wait for a check.
secondSetPieces.sector-7-b.title: Number transfers
secondSetPieces.sector-7-b.prompt: The intruder may be able to move customers' phone numbers to another network, and with them their sign-in codes.
secondSetPieces.sector-7-b.a.title: Suspend number transfers
secondSetPieces.sector-7-b.a.detail: No customer can move their number for a day, and the regulator is told why.
secondSetPieces.sector-7-b.b.title: Keep transfers open
secondSetPieces.sector-7-b.b.detail: Customers move numbers as normal while the route is traced.
secondSetPieces.sector-7-b.c.title: Call back before every transfer
secondSetPieces.sector-7-b.c.detail: Transfers continue, and each request is confirmed with the customer on their registered number.
secondSetPieces.sector-8-b.title: Chemical dosing values
secondSetPieces.sector-8-b.prompt: Dosing values were changed overnight. They are within safe limits, and nobody on shift remembers changing them.
secondSetPieces.sector-8-b.a.title: Restore the signed-off values and lock them
secondSetPieces.sector-8-b.a.detail: Operators put back the last approved values and block remote changes.
secondSetPieces.sector-8-b.b.title: Leave the values and watch
secondSetPieces.sector-8-b.b.detail: The plant runs as it is while the change is traced.
secondSetPieces.sector-8-b.c.title: Restore the values, keep remote access
secondSetPieces.sector-8-b.c.detail: The approved values return; remote changes stay possible, and each one raises an alarm.
secondSetPieces.sector-9-b.title: Treasury payment file
secondSetPieces.sector-9-b.prompt: Treasury's end-of-day payment file arrived with a changed list of payees, approved by the usual approver.
secondSetPieces.sector-9-b.a.title: Reject the file
secondSetPieces.sector-9-b.a.detail: Nothing in the file pays out; treasury resubmits after checking, past the cut-off.
secondSetPieces.sector-9-b.b.title: Release the file
secondSetPieces.sector-9-b.b.detail: Payments go on time to a payee list nobody has checked.
secondSetPieces.sector-9-b.c.title: Release, holding the new payees
secondSetPieces.sector-9-b.c.detail: Known payees are paid on time; new ones wait for a call back to treasury.
