campaignRoutes.breakwater.title: Breakwater
campaignRoutes.breakwater.order: Disrupt trusted access before the campaign reaches essential services.
campaignRoutes.breakwater.consequence: Lower starting impact, but intervention costs reduce service readiness.
campaignRoutes.common-ground.title: Common Ground
campaignRoutes.common-ground.order: Coordinate partners and protect shared operational confidence.
campaignRoutes.common-ground.consequence: Specialists recover faster and leadership trust matters more.
campaignRoutes.convergence.title: Convergence
campaignRoutes.convergence.order: Bring every confirmed thread into a single final operating picture.
campaignRoutes.convergence.consequence: The ending now reflects route, team cohesion and unresolved access.

injects.expert.title: A specialist joins
injects.expert.text: A responder helps focus the next investigative plan.
injects.expert.effectLabel: Analytical advantage on the next procedure.
injects.delay.title: Access approval delayed
injects.delay.text: Coordination friction slows the next action while business impact grows.
injects.delay.effectLabel: The next action is harder and pressure rises.
injects.restored.title: Collection pipeline restored
injects.restored.text: A repaired pipeline lets you revisit a used procedure early.
injects.partner.title: Partner shares evidence
injects.partner.text: A trusted partner supplies a validated finding.
injects.partner.effectLabel: One hidden stage is revealed, if any remain.
injects.press.title: Leadership wants an update
injects.press.text: Leaders ask whether the essential service is safe. Uncertainty carries a cost.
injects.backup.title: A useful evidence copy
injects.backup.text: Retained telemetry improves the next investigation.
injects.backup.effectLabel: Analytical advantage on the next procedure.
injects.noise.title: An alert flood
injects.noise.text: Unrelated alerts reduce analyst attention and delay decisions.
injects.noise.effectLabel: The next action is harder and pressure rises.
injects.operations.title: Operations stabilises service
injects.operations.text: A workaround buys the investigation team time.
injects.exercise.title: Authorised exercise confirmed
injects.exercise.text: The controller confirms that the activity belongs to an authorised test.
injects.logs.title: Retention extended
injects.logs.text: The storage team extends log retention before older records roll off.
injects.workaround.title: A manual workaround holds
injects.workaround.text: Staff run part of the service by hand while the systems are checked.
injects.blocked.title: Provider blocks an address
injects.blocked.text: An upstream provider blocks an address the intruder was using to reach the network.
injects.outage.title: An unrelated outage
injects.outage.text: A failed storage array takes part of the service down and pulls engineers away.
injects.rumour.title: A rumour spreads
injects.rumour.text: A staff post about “the hack” is shared outside the organisation.
injects.tipped.title: The intruder notices
injects.tipped.text: Collection traffic touched something the intruder was watching.
injects.absent.title: A key engineer is off sick
injects.absent.text: The engineer who knows the core system best is unavailable today.
injects.update.title: An update breaks a collector
injects.update.text: An overnight update stops a collection agent reporting, and the fix takes engineers off the service.
injects.update.effectLabel: The next action is harder and the service loses ground.
injects.audit.title: Internal audit sits in
injects.audit.text: An auditor joins the room: a second pair of eyes, and more questions to answer.
injects.audit.effectLabel: The next action is easier; business pressure rises.
injects.quiet.title: The intruder goes quiet
injects.quiet.text: Activity stops for an hour. The adversary is moving more slowly, and there is less to see.
injects.quiet.effectLabel: The adversary's pace slows; the next action is harder.
injects.overtime.title: Overtime approved
injects.overtime.text: Analysts stay late on the case, and the service desk runs short.
injects.overtime.effectLabel: The next action is easier; the service loses ground.
adversaryProfiles.ghost.title: Glass Viper
adversaryProfiles.ghost.description: Avoids recently examined evidence sources and favours identity or cloud trust.
adversaryProfiles.ghost.unverifiedSignal: A low-confidence identity alert may be operational noise or deliberate distraction.
adversaryProfiles.ghost.counterplay: Rotate evidence sources and avoid repeating the same collection pattern.
adversaryProfiles.raider.title: Red Quarry
adversaryProfiles.raider.description: Pushes execution and movement quickly when the response hesitates.
adversaryProfiles.raider.unverifiedSigna: A burst of endpoint alerts is credible, but its relationship to the original access remains unproven.
adversaryProfiles.raider.counterplay: Reveal a stage or intervene before each second action.
adversaryProfiles.broker.title: Black Relay
adversaryProfiles.broker.description: Blends into supplier, application and shared-service relationships.
adversaryProfiles.broker.unverifiedSigna: A partner-originated event overlaps the timeline but has not been causally linked.
adversaryProfiles.broker.counterplay: Use focused checks on supplier and shared-service boundaries.
adversaryProfiles.ledger.title: Cipher Ledger
adversaryProfiles.ledger.description: Targets approval paths, privileged identities and transaction systems for financial effect.
adversaryProfiles.ledger.unverifiedSigna: A suspicious approval pattern may be fraud, process error or deliberate misdirection.
adversaryProfiles.ledger.counterplay: Maintain a working theory and avoid rapid analysis on approval paths.
adversaryProfiles.sentinel.title: Silent Meridian
adversaryProfiles.sentinel.description: Maps operational dependencies and preserves access for a future strategic objective.
adversaryProfiles.sentinel.unverifiedSig: Low-volume discovery activity suggests mapping, but its intended use remains unclear.
adversaryProfiles.sentinel.counterplay: Protect sector health while testing operational dependencies.
adversaryProfiles.lantern.title: Grey Lantern
adversaryProfiles.lantern.description: Settles into systems nobody is watching and waits for them to stay unwatched.
adversaryProfiles.lantern.unverifiedSign: An old maintenance account signed in overnight. It may be a scheduled job, or someone using it.
adversaryProfiles.lantern.counterplay: Use the infrastructure map early: monitor or isolate a system before the third turn.
adversaryProfiles.choir.title: Hollow Choir
adversaryProfiles.choir.description: Spreads its activity across systems so that each finding looks unrelated to the last.
adversaryProfiles.choir.unverifiedSignal: Two alerts on separate systems arrived minutes apart. They may be one actor or two unrelated faults.
adversaryProfiles.choir.counterplay: Compare confirmed findings as soon as two stand; an untested pair is what it relies on.
adversaryProfiles.ember.title: Ember Shift
adversaryProfiles.ember.description: Times its moves to service strain, when responders are busiest and least watchful.
adversaryProfiles.ember.unverifiedSignal: A surge of service-desk tickets coincides with the activity. It may be cover, or coincidence.
adversaryProfiles.ember.counterplay: Keep service continuity above 60; below it, the strain covers the actor's moves.
commandEvents.scope.title: Scope is expanding
commandEvents.scope.prompt: A connected service reports related activity. Decide how broadly the team should investigate.
commandEvents.scope.a.title: Expand the evidence boundary
commandEvents.scope.a.description: Bring the connected service into the investigation now.
commandEvents.scope.a.signal: Wider scope, added pressure · Next roll harder
commandEvents.scope.b.title: Hold the current boundary
commandEvents.scope.b.description: Keep the team focused until the link is confirmed.
commandEvents.scope.b.signal: Next roll easier · More pressure, faster adversary
commandEvents.leadership.title: Leadership needs a recommendation
commandEvents.leadership.prompt: Executives need a clear position before the next operational decision.
commandEvents.leadership.a.title: Brief confirmed facts and uncertainty
commandEvents.leadership.a.description: State what is known, what is assumed and what decision is approaching.
commandEvents.leadership.b.title: Delay until the picture is complete
commandEvents.leadership.b.description: Preserve analyst time and wait for stronger attribution.
commandEvents.leadership.b.signal: Next roll easier · Pressure rises, faster adversary
commandEvents.capacity.title: Specialist capacity is limited
commandEvents.capacity.prompt: One specialist team can be surged into the incident, but routine operations will lose support.
commandEvents.capacity.a.title: Surge specialist support
commandEvents.capacity.a.description: Accelerate the next evidence action and accept operational strain.
commandEvents.capacity.b.title: Preserve operational coverage
commandEvents.capacity.b.description: Keep routine services supported and continue with the current team.
commandEvents.capacity.b.signal: Continuity protected · Pressure rises, faster adversary
commandEvents.counsel.title: Counsel asks to direct the collection
commandEvents.counsel.prompt: Legal counsel wants evidence gathered under their direction so findings stay privileged if the incident reaches court.
commandEvents.counsel.a.title: Route collection through counsel
commandEvents.counsel.a.description: Findings are documented for counsel first, which slows the next check but steadies the organisation.
commandEvents.counsel.b.title: Collect now and brief counsel after
commandEvents.counsel.b.description: Keep the investigation moving and accept that some findings may be harder to defend later.
commandEvents.supplier.title: A supplier offers remote help
commandEvents.supplier.prompt: The vendor of an affected system offers an engineer on a remote session today. Their access would be one more way in.
commandEvents.supplier.a.title: Accept a supervised session
commandEvents.supplier.a.description: The engineer knows the system and speeds the next check, but a new remote path is open while they work.
commandEvents.supplier.b.title: Decline and work with the team you have
commandEvents.supplier.b.description: No new access while the intruder is inside, at the cost of a slower, more anxious organisation.
commandEvents.regulator.title: A regulator asks whether to expect a notice
commandEvents.regulator.prompt: The sector regulator has heard about the disruption and asks whether a formal notification is coming.
commandEvents.regulator.a.title: File an early factual notice
commandEvents.regulator.a.description: Say what is known and what is not. The regulator is reassured; drafting it costs analyst time.
commandEvents.regulator.b.title: Wait until the scope is confirmed
commandEvents.regulator.b.description: Keep the analysts on the investigation and answer the regulator later.
commandEvents.shift.title: The night shift is exhausted
commandEvents.shift.prompt: The analysts who have worked the incident since it began have been awake for twenty hours.
commandEvents.shift.a.title: Hand over to a fresh shift
commandEvents.shift.a.description: A rested team makes fewer mistakes, but the handover loses some of what the first team knew.
commandEvents.shift.b.title: Push on with the current shift
commandEvents.shift.b.description: They know the incident best; tired people also miss things and lose the room's confidence.
commandEvents.media.title: A journalist has heard about the outage
commandEvents.media.prompt: A reporter is asking whether the disruption is a cyber attack and plans to publish within the hour.
commandEvents.media.a.title: Issue a short holding statement
commandEvents.media.a.description: Confirm an incident is being handled without detail. Staff are pulled onto customer questions.
commandEvents.media.b.title: Decline to comment
commandEvents.media.b.description: Nothing is said that might be wrong, and the story runs without the organisation's account.
commandEvents.backups.title: Backups may be reachable from the intrusion
commandEvents.backups.prompt: The backup servers share credentials with systems the intruder may control. If they are wiped, recovery gets much harder.
commandEvents.backups.a.title: Take the backups offline now
commandEvents.backups.a.description: Protects the recovery point, and stops the jobs that keep some services running.
commandEvents.backups.b.title: Leave them online and watch them
commandEvents.backups.b.description: Every access to the backups becomes evidence, and the intruder keeps a target.
commandEvents.backups.b.signal: Next roll easier · Faster adversary · Pressure rises
commandEvents.approach.title: Someone was asked for their sign-in code
commandEvents.approach.prompt: A member of staff reports a call from “the help desk” asking for the code on their phone. They did not give it.
commandEvents.approach.a.title: Treat it as part of the incident
commandEvents.approach.a.description: Trace the call and the account it targeted; the intruder may be trying another way in.
commandEvents.approach.b.title: Log it for the security awareness team
commandEvents.approach.b.description: Keep the investigation on the evidence already in hand.
commandEvents.change.title: A scheduled change is due tonight
commandEvents.change.prompt: A planned upgrade to an affected system is booked for tonight. Postponing it disappoints the service owner.
commandEvents.change.a.title: Freeze all changes
commandEvents.change.a.description: Systems stay as they are while evidence is collected, and the upgrade's improvements wait.
commandEvents.change.b.title: Let the change go ahead
commandEvents.change.b.description: The service gets its upgrade; the systems under investigation change underneath the team.
commandEvents.forensics.title: An outside forensics team can start in an hour
commandEvents.forensics.prompt: A retained incident-response firm has a team free now. Bringing them in is expensive and visible.
commandEvents.forensics.a.title: Engage the outside team
commandEvents.forensics.a.description: Experienced hands for the next check; the cost and the extra people raise the temperature.
commandEvents.forensics.b.title: Keep the investigation in house
commandEvents.forensics.b.description: No cost and no new faces, and the team works at the pace it has.
commandEvents.insurer.title: The insurer wants its own responders
commandEvents.insurer.prompt: The cyber insurer will cover the response only if its approved firm takes part.
commandEvents.insurer.a.title: Bring in the insurer's firm
commandEvents.insurer.a.description: The cost is covered and the board is reassured; the handover slows the next check.
commandEvents.insurer.b.title: Keep the current team and inform the insurer
commandEvents.insurer.b.description: No handover, and a dispute about the bill that the board will hear about.
commandEvents.phished.title: A member of staff reports a suspicious page
commandEvents.phished.prompt: Someone in finance says they typed their password into a page that looked wrong, last week.
commandEvents.phished.a.title: Reset their account and trace its use
commandEvents.phished.a.description: Their sign-ins become evidence, and they lose access for the afternoon.
commandEvents.phished.b.title: Note it and carry on
commandEvents.phished.b.description: The investigation keeps its course, and an account that may be in use stays open.
commandEvents.claim.title: Someone claims responsibility
commandEvents.claim.prompt: A message to the press office claims responsibility for the incident and names one of your systems.
commandEvents.claim.a.title: Check the named system
commandEvents.claim.a.description: It may be a lead or a distraction; either way the press office has questions now.
commandEvents.claim.b.title: Pass it to the police and keep to the evidence
commandEvents.claim.b.description: The message is handled properly, and the team does not chase it.
commandEvents.segment.title: The network team can cut a segment
commandEvents.segment.prompt: The affected part of the network can be cut off from the rest within the hour.
commandEvents.segment.a.title: Cut the segment now
commandEvents.segment.a.description: Whatever is inside it is stranded, and so are the people who work there.
commandEvents.segment.b.title: Leave it connected and watch it
commandEvents.segment.b.description: Every connection becomes evidence, and the intruder keeps its route out.
commandEvents.storage.title: Log storage is nearly full
commandEvents.storage.prompt: The log store will start overwriting its oldest records tonight.
commandEvents.storage.a.title: Buy emergency storage
commandEvents.storage.a.description: The records are kept, and finance wants to know why the budget moved.
commandEvents.storage.b.title: Let the oldest records roll off
commandEvents.storage.b.description: No cost, and the start of the incident may go with them.
commandEvents.customer.title: A major customer asks for a call
commandEvents.customer.prompt: Your largest customer wants to hear directly what is happening and whether they are affected.
commandEvents.customer.a.title: Brief them now
commandEvents.customer.a.description: The customer is steadier for it, and the call takes the lead analyst for an hour.
commandEvents.customer.b.title: Send a written update
commandEvents.customer.b.description: The team keeps working, and the customer reads a short note as a brush-off.
responseProfiles.0.constraint: Business confidence margin: isolating the shared application tier interrupts payroll and dependent workflows first.
responseProfiles.0.containment.isolate.d: Severs the trust path to shared applications and stops dependent workflows.
responseProfiles.0.containment.credentia: Constrains identity-led movement across payroll and shared services.
responseProfiles.0.containment.monitor.d: Preserves payroll availability while the actor retains opportunity.
responseProfiles.0.assurance.verify.desc: Test identities, integrations and dependencies before restoration.
responseProfiles.0.assurance.preserve.de: Retain approval, identity and application artefacts before change.
Payroll and workflow owners can see their own data, so their sign-off carries real weight here.
responseProfiles.0.recovery.rebuild.titl: Rebuild the application tier from baseline
responseProfiles.0.recovery.rebuild.desc: Highest assurance for shared services, with the longest payroll interruption.
responseProfiles.0.recovery.restore.desc: Returns payroll and shared applications faster if integrity is understood.
responseProfiles.0.recovery.patch.title: Patch the application tier in place
responseProfiles.0.recovery.patch.descri: A shared application tier patches cleanly and the dependency map is well understood.
responseProfiles.1.constraint: Clinical service margin: containment cuts deepest here, and every isolation must be justified against care delivery.
responseProfiles.1.containment.isolate.t: Isolate the support path serving clinical work
responseProfiles.1.containment.isolate.d: Stops support access and suspends scheduling and records for care teams.
responseProfiles.1.containment.credentia: Constrains support access with limited interruption to care delivery.
responseProfiles.1.containment.monitor.d: Preserves clinical continuity while the actor retains opportunity.
responseProfiles.1.assurance.verify.desc: Prove identities, routes and dependent workflows before restoration.
responseProfiles.1.assurance.preserve.de: Keep the forensic images taken before containment so the restored path can be verified against them.
Care teams verify records against their own independent checks, and every hour of manual working carries its own risk.
responseProfiles.1.recovery.rebuild.titl: Rebuild the support estate from baseline
responseProfiles.1.recovery.rebuild.desc: Highest assurance, with the longest period of manual clinical work.
responseProfiles.1.recovery.restore.desc: Returns scheduling and records faster if integrity is sound.
responseProfiles.1.recovery.patch.title: Patch in place under clinical supervision
responseProfiles.1.recovery.patch.descri: Keeps scheduling and records running while clinicians watch for anomalies they would recognise.
responseProfiles.2.constraint: Operational support integrity: successful boundary analysis protects support, but isolation erodes engineering capacity.
responseProfiles.2.containment.isolate.d: Removes remote support and leaves local engineers covering operations.
responseProfiles.2.containment.credentia: Constrains the support trust path while local administration continues.
responseProfiles.2.containment.monitor.d: Preserves engineering support while accepting continued actor access.
responseProfiles.2.assurance.verify.desc: Test supplier routes and support dependencies before restoration.
responseProfiles.2.assurance.preserve.de: Retain jump-host and configuration evidence before change.
Plant instrumentation is independent of the support estate, so it can confirm what the support estate cannot.
responseProfiles.2.recovery.rebuild.titl: Rebuild the support estate from baseline
responseProfiles.2.recovery.rebuild.desc: Strongest assurance, with the longest engineering-capacity gap.
responseProfiles.2.recovery.restore.desc: Returns maintenance capability faster if integrity is understood.
responseProfiles.2.recovery.patch.title: Patch in place behind the plant boundary
responseProfiles.2.recovery.patch.descri: The engineering boundary holds while the support estate is patched, and the independent safety system and local field readings would show a deviation that a compromised engineering path could not hide.
responseProfiles.3.constraint: Terminal schedule margin: capacity falls fastest late in the incident, and isolation severs partner transactions first.
responseProfiles.3.containment.isolate.d: Cuts external partner access and shifts bookings to manual handling.
responseProfiles.3.containment.credentia: Constrains the portal trust path with limited terminal disruption.
responseProfiles.3.containment.monitor.t: Monitor the portal while mapping scope
responseProfiles.3.containment.monitor.d: Preserves terminal throughput while partner risk persists.
responseProfiles.3.assurance.verify.desc: Test portal identities and planning dependencies before restoration.
responseProfiles.3.assurance.preserve.de: Retain portal and scheduling artefacts before the platform changes.
Terminal checks confirm that bookings flow, not that they are trustworthy, and partner traffic keeps moving either way.
responseProfiles.3.recovery.rebuild.titl: Rebuild the booking platform from baseline
responseProfiles.3.recovery.rebuild.desc: Highest assurance, with the longest planning interruption.
responseProfiles.3.recovery.restore.desc: Returns automated planning faster if integrity is sound.
responseProfiles.3.recovery.patch.title: Patch in place and keep the berth working
responseProfiles.3.recovery.patch.descri: Holds terminal capacity, but partner systems keep transacting against an estate you have not re-proved.
responseProfiles.4.constraint: Tenant trust boundary: control-plane exposure widens tenant risk, and unapproved scope advances the actor's objective.
responseProfiles.4.containment.isolate.d: Stops the privilege path to tenant resources and disrupts shared workloads.
responseProfiles.4.containment.credentia: Constrains control-plane access while dependent automation keeps running.
responseProfiles.4.containment.monitor.d: Preserves workload availability while the privilege path stays open.
responseProfiles.4.assurance.verify.desc: Test roles, trust policies and derived keys before restoration.
responseProfiles.4.assurance.preserve.de: Retain audit history and key material before roles change.
The provider attests to a control plane you cannot inspect, which is the plane under investigation.
responseProfiles.4.recovery.rebuild.titl: Rebuild the workload from a trusted image
responseProfiles.4.recovery.rebuild.desc: Highest assurance, with the longest automation gap.
responseProfiles.4.recovery.restore.desc: Returns automation faster if snapshot integrity is understood.
responseProfiles.4.recovery.patch.title: Patch roles in place and monitor
responseProfiles.4.recovery.patch.descri: Keeps workloads running, but a role left in place is the same role the actor used.
responseProfiles.5.constraint: Shared-service confidence: unverified trust propagates to dependent organisations, so scope and notification shape the outcome.
responseProfiles.5.containment.isolate.d: Severs the single trust entry point and affects every connected organisation.
responseProfiles.5.containment.credentia: Constrains the shared trust path while connected services keep operating.
responseProfiles.5.containment.monitor.d: Preserves dependent services while the shared trust stays unverified.
responseProfiles.5.assurance.verify.desc: Prove the trust service and federation routes before restoration.
responseProfiles.5.assurance.preserve.de: Retain federation and identity artefacts before change.
Downstream tenants sign off on their own view, which leaves what they cannot see unexamined.
responseProfiles.5.recovery.rebuild.titl: Rebuild the shared platform from baseline
responseProfiles.5.recovery.rebuild.desc: Strongest assurance, with the longest coordination pause for partners.
responseProfiles.5.recovery.restore.desc: Returns dependent organisations faster if integrity is understood.
responseProfiles.5.recovery.patch.title: Patch the shared platform in place
responseProfiles.5.recovery.patch.descri: A shared platform is patched once for every tenant, and staged rollout is routine work here.
responseProfiles.6.constraint: Public transaction capacity: public demand constrains disruptive containment, and a communications lead protects capacity.
responseProfiles.6.containment.isolate.d: Cuts privileged access and interrupts in-flight citizen transactions.
responseProfiles.6.containment.credentia: Constrains the privileged path while public transactions continue.
responseProfiles.6.containment.monitor.d: Preserves the transaction window while administrative risk persists.
responseProfiles.6.assurance.verify.desc: Prove administrative routes and agency dependencies before restoration.
responseProfiles.6.assurance.preserve.de: Retain identity and application artefacts before change.
Service checks show the counter is open. The authority to make administrative decisions is what is in question.
responseProfiles.6.recovery.rebuild.titl: Rebuild the public service from baseline
responseProfiles.6.recovery.rebuild.desc: Highest assurance, with the longest administrative pause.
responseProfiles.6.recovery.restore.desc: Returns citizen transactions faster if integrity is sound.
responseProfiles.6.recovery.patch.title: Patch in place and keep services open
responseProfiles.6.recovery.patch.descri: Public capacity holds, but administrative decisions keep issuing from an estate still under suspicion.
responseProfiles.7.constraint: Core network stability: the core decays fastest of all sectors, and containment must avoid unnecessary loss of connectivity.
responseProfiles.7.containment.isolate.d: Removes the management path and risks national connectivity.
responseProfiles.7.containment.credentia: Constrains the management plane while subscriber traffic continues.
responseProfiles.7.containment.monitor.d: Preserves connectivity while the actor keeps management access.
responseProfiles.7.assurance.verify.desc: Test routing control and management routes before restoration.
responseProfiles.7.assurance.preserve.de: Retain routing and management artefacts before change.
A compromised management plane reports healthy routing, because reporting healthy routing is what it is for.
responseProfiles.7.recovery.rebuild.titl: Rebuild the management core from baseline
responseProfiles.7.recovery.rebuild.desc: Strongest assurance, with the longest restriction of management change.
responseProfiles.7.recovery.restore.desc: Returns routing control faster if integrity is understood.
responseProfiles.7.recovery.patch.title: Patch the management plane in place
responseProfiles.7.recovery.patch.descri: Connectivity holds and the change window stays short, but the plane doing the reporting is the one being patched.
responseProfiles.8.constraint: Process safety margin: the margin resists delay, but unapproved scope and any isolation erode it sharply.
responseProfiles.8.containment.isolate.d: Removes support access and moves one process area to manual supervision.
responseProfiles.8.containment.credentia: Constrains support access while operations continue under normal control.
responseProfiles.8.containment.monitor.d: Preserves the operating envelope while engineering trust stays uncertain.
responseProfiles.8.assurance.verify.desc: Test vendor routes and engineering dependencies before restoration.
responseProfiles.8.assurance.preserve.de: Retain historian and configuration artefacts before change.
Manual supervision and physical process limits sit outside the compromised estate and can be trusted on their own terms.
responseProfiles.8.recovery.rebuild.titl: Rebuild the support environment from baseline
responseProfiles.8.recovery.rebuild.desc: Strongest assurance, with the longest manual-supervision period.
responseProfiles.8.recovery.restore.desc: Returns engineering support faster if integrity is understood.
responseProfiles.8.recovery.patch.title: Patch in place under manual supervision
responseProfiles.8.recovery.patch.descri: Supervision continues through the patch, checked against the independent safety system and local field readings rather than the screens the attacker may have touched.
responseProfiles.9.constraint: Clearing-window integrity: integrity erodes with delay and failure, and every decision must be defensible before settlement.
responseProfiles.9.containment.isolate.d: Cuts the approval path and suspends in-flight settlement.
responseProfiles.9.containment.credentia: Constrains the approval plane while settlement continues under review.
responseProfiles.9.containment.monitor.d: Preserves the settlement window while approval integrity is unverified.
responseProfiles.9.assurance.verify.desc: Test approvals, roles and settlement dependencies before restoration.
responseProfiles.9.assurance.preserve.de: Retain transaction and approval artefacts before change.
Reconciliation is the control being tested. Accepting its own output as assurance is the failure this incident is about.
responseProfiles.9.recovery.rebuild.titl: Rebuild the clearing service from baseline
responseProfiles.9.recovery.rebuild.desc: Highest assurance, with the longest settlement delay.
responseProfiles.9.recovery.restore.desc: Returns clearing faster if backup integrity is understood.
responseProfiles.9.recovery.patch.title: Patch in place and clear the window
responseProfiles.9.recovery.patch.descri: The settlement window closes on time, on an estate whose approval path has not been re-proved.
decisionLanguage.0.observe: Keep the suspected route active long enough to correlate its origin.
decisionLanguage.0.act: Terminate the observed access and invalidate related sessions.
decisionLanguage.0.attribute: Correlate the access with prior behaviour and artefacts before changing anything.
decisionLanguage.0.contain: Restrict the observed path to a bounded trust scope, keeping {service} running.
decisionLanguage.0.notify: Brief leadership and {owners} on confirmed facts before the next action.
decisionLanguage.1.observe: Watch the movement briefly to identify reached systems and identities.
decisionLanguage.1.act: Block the observed administrative route before scope is complete.
decisionLanguage.1.attribute: Map the identities and systems touched, and compare them with the actor's established behaviour.
decisionLanguage.1.contain: Segment the observed route at the nearest trust boundary, keeping {service} running.
decisionLanguage.1.notify: Tell {owners} which systems were reached, what is confirmed and what remains uncertain.
decisionLanguage.2.observe: Preserve volatile and configuration evidence before removal.
decisionLanguage.2.act: Disable the confirmed mechanism and accept reduced visibility.
decisionLanguage.2.attribute: Identify the mechanism, its authoring pattern and any related access before removal.
decisionLanguage.2.contain: Disable the observed mechanism on a bounded set of systems, keeping {service} running.
decisionLanguage.2.notify: Brief {owners} on the confirmed mechanism and the change window its removal needs.
decisionLanguage.3.observe: Collect destination and transfer evidence before blocking it.
decisionLanguage.3.act: Stop the confirmed connection before attribution and scope are complete.
decisionLanguage.3.attribute: Correlate destination, timing and volume to characterise the channel before blocking it.
decisionLanguage.3.contain: Throttle and restrict the observed channel at the boundary rather than cutting every connection {service} relies on.
decisionLanguage.3.notify: Inform {owners} and compliance of the confirmed export path and its uncertainty.

decisionEffects.observe: Evidence improved while attacker opportunity increased.

debriefQuestionSets.reading.title: Reading the route
debriefQuestionSets.reading.purpose: For a group that lost to the window, or kept one reading too long.
debriefQuestionSets.reading.questions.0: At which stage did your reading stop matching what the team was seeing, and what on the board said so first?
debriefQuestionSets.reading.questions.1: Which check that found nothing ruled the most out, and did you use what it ruled out?
debriefQuestionSets.reading.questions.2: When a source shared between routes found a later stage, what did that tell you about the stage you were testing, and what did it not?
debriefQuestionSets.reading.questions.3: If you played this stage again, which single check would you run first, and why that one?
debriefQuestionSets.decisions.title: Decisions under pressure
debriefQuestionSets.decisions.purpose: For a group whose evidence decisions or sector crisis shaped the result.
Which decision traded the most service for the least certainty, and would the people who run that service have agreed?
Where did watching longer pay off, and where did it hand the adversary time?
Who in a real organisation would have owned the sector decision, and who would they have needed in the room?
Which choice would you defend to a regulator the next morning, and which would you rather not?
debriefQuestionSets.response.title: Response and recovery
debriefQuestionSets.response.purpose: For a group that reached the response, or won and wants to know whether it was the right win.
debriefQuestionSets.response.questions.0: Did the containment you chose close the access the chain showed, or only the part you could see?
debriefQuestionSets.response.questions.1: What did assurance check, and what would have happened had you skipped it?
debriefQuestionSets.response.questions.2: Was the recovery you chose the one that removes the adversary's foothold, or the fastest one back to service?
debriefQuestionSets.response.questions.3: What would your organisation need, that it does not have today, to make the same call in the same time?
difficultyTeaches.training: The loop: declare a reading, test it with one of its own sources, revise when the board says it is weakening, and compare two confirmed findings. A clue at each stage keeps the first reading from being a guess, and the board marks what checks have ruled out.
difficultyTeaches.operational: Reading the route without the clue. The standing and the ruled-out marks remain, so a group learns to reason from what checks have excluded rather than from a hint.
difficultyTeaches.crisis: Judgement under pressure: fewer map actions, a faster adversary that re-routes the stage after the one under test, and a shorter window. The reasoning is the same; the cost of a slow or unsound reading is higher.
plainLanguage.endpoint: An individual computer — a laptop, desktop or server — as opposed to the network or an online service.
plainLanguage.control plane: The management layer of a cloud service: the settings, roles and keys that decide what everything else in the account may do.
plainLanguage.pivot: Using one compromised system or account as a stepping stone to reach the next.
plainLanguage.C2: Command and control: the channel an intruder uses to send instructions to compromised systems and receive what they collect.
plainLanguage.egress: Traffic leaving the organisation's network for the internet.
plainLanguage.east-west traffic: Traffic between systems inside the network, rather than in from or out to the internet.
plainLanguage.DNS: The internet's address book, which turns names into network addresses. Its lookups can be abused to smuggle small amounts of data.
plainLanguage.established source: An evidence source your team already knows well: a few start that way and the campaign adds more. It adds +2 to the roll.
plainLanguage.inject: An unplanned event the exercise controller adds part-way through: a disclosure, an outage or a lucky break.
plainLanguage.pre-positioning: Gaining quiet access now in order to act later, often during a crisis, rather than to take anything today.
plainLanguage.telemetry: The records systems produce on their own about what they are doing: logs, alerts and traffic data.
plainLanguage.credential: Anything that proves who you are to a system: a password, a key, a token or a certificate.
plainLanguage.service ticket: A time-limited pass a network's sign-in service hands out so an account can use one particular system.
plainLanguage.TXT record: A free-text entry in the internet's naming system; it can be abused to carry small pieces of data in and out.
plainLanguage.logon script: A small program that runs automatically when someone signs in to a computer.
plainLanguage.delegated access: Permission one account gives another to act on its behalf, such as reading its mailbox.
plainLanguage.unsigned payload: A program or file with no maker's signature, so nothing vouches for where it came from.
plainLanguage.MFA: Multi-factor authentication: a second check at sign-in, such as a phone prompt, on top of the password.
plainLanguage.federation: An arrangement where one organisation's sign-in service is trusted by another's, so one account works across both.
plainLanguage.historian: The database that records an industrial plant's readings over time.
plainLanguage.SaaS: Software as a service: an application the organisation uses over the internet rather than running itself.
plainLanguage.webhook: An address one service calls automatically to tell another that something happened.
plainLanguage.snapshot: A point-in-time copy of a disk or system.
plainLanguage.token: A digital pass a system issues after sign-in, so a person or program need not sign in again for every request.
plainLanguage.artefacts: Traces a program leaves behind on a computer — files, settings and memory — that investigators can examine.
plainLanguage.API: A way for programs to talk to a service directly, without a person clicking through screens.
plainLanguage.payload: The part of an attack or a message that does the actual work, such as the data or code being carried.
plainLanguage.workload: A program or job running in the cloud, usually on its own with no person at the keyboard.
plainLanguage.beaconing: A compromised computer checking in with the intruder at regular intervals for new instructions.
plainLanguage.resolver: The service that answers DNS lookups, turning a name into the address behind it.
plainLanguage.process ancestry: Which program started which: the chain of parent and child programs that led to an action.
plainLanguage.privileged tier: Accounts with powerful administrative access — the ones that can change anything.
plainLanguage.trust boundary: The line between two systems that are allowed to rely on each other. Crossing it is how an intruder spreads.
plainLanguage.actor tempo: How quickly the intruder is moving. It rises when you give them time and falls when you press them.
plainLanguage.bounded containment: Shutting down one specific path rather than the whole service, so less of the business stops.
plainLanguage.assurance gate: The step between stopping the attack and restoring service, where you check the environment is actually clean.
plainLanguage.residual risk: What is still uncertain after you act — the part of the problem the chosen option does not settle.
plainLanguage.causal sequence: One finding is what the next one needed — consecutive stages of the intrusion, or two steps on the same route. Two things on the same system at the same time are not thereby related.
plainLanguage.evidence boundary: How far out you are currently looking. Widening it brings connected systems into the investigation and costs time.
plainLanguage.assurance: Checking the environment is genuinely clean before you put the service back.
plainLanguage.exfiltration: Data being taken out of the organisation.
plainLanguage.persistence: A foothold the intruder can return through after a reboot or a password change.
plainLanguage.lateral movement: Moving from the first system compromised to other systems inside the network.
plainLanguage.attribution: Working out who is behind the activity, from how they behave rather than from a name.
plainLanguage.continuity: Whether the essential service is still running for the people who depend on it.
plainLanguage.VPN: A remote-access connection that puts an outside computer onto the organisation's network as if it were inside.
plainLanguage.OT: Operational technology: the computers that run physical equipment such as pumps, valves, cranes and power switching.
plainLanguage.OSS: Operations support systems: the software a telecoms operator uses to set up and manage its customers' services.
plainLanguage.phishing: A message made to look genuine so that someone opens an attachment, follows a link or gives away a password.
plainLanguage.password spraying: Trying a few common passwords against many accounts, slowly, so that no single account locks.
plainLanguage.privilege escalation: Gaining more access than the account or program started with, usually administrator rights.
plainLanguage.jump host: A computer staff are meant to pass through to reach a protected network; whoever controls it can reach what it reaches.
plainLanguage.web shell: A small file placed on a web server that lets an outsider run commands through ordinary web requests.
plainLanguage.implant: Malicious software placed on a computer to give the intruder lasting control of it.
plainLanguage.tunnel: A connection carried inside another, so traffic that would be blocked travels hidden in traffic that is allowed.
plainLanguage.proxy: A computer that passes traffic on for others, so the real source and destination are hidden from each end.
plainLanguage.port forward: Redirecting traffic arriving at one computer on to another, often to reach a network the outsider cannot reach directly.
plainLanguage.covert channel: A way of moving data hidden inside something that looks routine, such as name lookups or web requests.
plainLanguage.dead drop: A public place, such as a web page or post, where the intruder leaves instructions for their software to collect.
plainLanguage.service account: An account used by a program rather than a person, often with wide access and rarely watched.
plainLanguage.scheduled task: A job a computer runs by itself at set times; an intruder uses one to restart their software.
plainLanguage.autorun: A setting that starts a program automatically when the computer starts or someone signs in.
plainLanguage.event subscription: An instruction for a computer to run something whenever a particular event happens.
plainLanguage.container image: The packaged template a cloud workload is started from; alter it and every copy starts altered.
plainLanguage.pipeline runner: The machine that builds and deploys software automatically, using credentials that can reach many systems.
plainLanguage.sideloaded: Installed by hand from outside the approved source, so the usual checks never saw it.
plainLanguage.segmentation: Dividing a network so that a problem in one part cannot easily reach the others.
plainLanguage.threat hunt: Searching for an intruder's behaviour across many sources, rather than waiting for an alert.
plainLanguage.forensic: Careful, recorded examination of a computer's contents to establish what happened and when.
plainLanguage.identity assertion: A signed statement from one system telling another who a user is, which the second trusts instead of checking.
plainLanguage.tenant: One customer's separate space inside a shared cloud or managed service.
plainLanguage.foothold: The first point of lasting access an intruder holds inside the organisation.
